48:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Fath It is a city Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mughaffal say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat al-Fath on his mount in the year of the conquest, and then he returned with it. Mu’awiyah said: Were it not that I hate for people to gather around us, I would have narrated his recitation. They both narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful This noble Surah was revealed when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Al-Hudaybiyah in Dhul-Qa’dah of the sixth year of the Hijrah, when the polytheists prevented him from reaching the Sacred Mosque to perform his Umrah there. They prevented him from doing so, then they leaned toward reconciliation and a truce, and that he would return this year and then come the next year. He agreed to that, despite the reluctance of a group of the Companions, including Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, as will be detailed in its place in the interpretation of this Surah, God willing. So when he slaughtered his sacrifice when he was prevented and returned, God, the Almighty, revealed this Surah from his command and their command, and made that peace treaty a conquest in consideration of the benefit in it and the outcome of the matter, as Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, and others narrated that he said: You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Mecca, and we consider the conquest to be the Treaty of Al-Hudaybiyah. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: We did not consider the conquest to be anything but the day of Al-Hudaybah. Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa told us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’, may God be pleased with him. He said: You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Mecca, but the conquest of Mecca was a conquest. We consider the conquest to be the Pledge of Ridwan on the day of Hudaybiyyah. We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fourteen hundred. Hudaybiyyah was a well, so we drained it and did not leave a drop in it. report of that reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he came to us and sat on its edge. Then he called for a vessel of water, performed ablution, rinsed his mouth and supplicated, then poured it into it. We left it not far away, then it sent forth whatever we and our mounts wished. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nuh told us, Malik bin Anas told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. He said: I asked him about something three times, but he did not answer me. He said: I said to myself: May your mother lose you, O son of Al-Khattab, you insisted and repeated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, three times, and he did not answer you? He said: So I mounted my mount and moved my camel forward, fearing that the revelation had been sent down concerning something. He said: Then I heard a caller call: O Umar! He said: So I went back, thinking that the revelation had been sent down concerning something. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Last night a surah was revealed to me that is dearer to me than the world and what is in it: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, * That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come.’” Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Malik may God have mercy on him. ‘Ali ibn Al-Madini said: This is a good Madani chain of transmission that we did not find except with them. Imam Ahmad said: ‘Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: “‘So God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come’ was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A verse has been revealed to me tonight that is dearer to me than anything on the earth. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited it to them and they said: “Congratulations and good report, O Prophet of God. God Almighty has made clear what He will do with you, so what will He do with us?” So the verse was revealed to him (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and He will remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, in the sight of God, a great attainment.” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Majma' bin Ya'qub told us: I heard my father narrating on the authority of his uncle Abd al-Rahman bin Yazid al-Ansari, on the authority of his uncle Majma' bin Haritha al-Ansari may God be pleased with him, who was one of the reciters of the Quran. He said: We witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah and when we left, the people were scaring the camels away. The people said to one another: What is wrong with the people? They said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was inspired to me, so we went out with the people, hurrying. Then, there was the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on his mount near Kura' al-Ghamim. The people gathered around him, and he recited to them: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. A man from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Which Messenger of God or conquest is this? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, by the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it is a conquest. So Khaybar was divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyyah. No one entered it with them except those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided it into eighteen shares. The army was one thousand five hundred, including three hundred horsemen. The horseman was given two shares and the foot soldier one share. Abu Dawud narrated it in Jihad on the authority of Muhammad bin Isa on the authority of Majma’ bin Ya’qub on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay` told us, Abu Bahr told us, Shu`bah told us, Jami` ibn Shaddad told us, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi `Ulqamah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas`ud may God be pleased with him say: When we returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah, we camped and slept, and we did not wake up until the sun had risen. We woke up and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was asleep. We said: Wake him up, and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) woke up and said: Do what you were doing, and this is what one does who sleeps or forgets. We missed the she-camel of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so we looked for it and found its halter caught in a tree. I brought it to him and he mounted it, and while we were walking, the revelation came to him. He said: Whenever the revelation came to him, it would be difficult for him, and when it was over, he informed us that the verse, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, had been revealed to him. Ahmad, Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Jami` ibn Shaddad. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Alaqah, who said: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray until his feet swelled. It was said to him: Has God not forgiven you your past and future sins? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Should I not be a grateful servant? They and the rest of the group narrated it, except for Abu Dawud, on the authority of Ziyad. Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Maruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Ibn Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed, he would stand until his feet would swell. Aisha may God be pleased with her said to him: O Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), do you do this when God has forgiven you your past and future sins? He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: O Aisha, should I not be a grateful servant? Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Awf Al-Kharraz - who was trustworthy in Makkah - Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Misa’ar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood until his feet - or he said his legs - swelled. It was said to him: Has God not forgiven you your past and future sins? He said: Should I not be a grateful servant? This is strange from this perspective. His saying: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest means clear and apparent. What is meant by it is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, because of it, abundant goodness occurred, people believed and gathered together, the believer spoke to the disbeliever, and beneficial knowledge and faith spread. And the Almighty’s saying: So that God may forgive you your past and future sins. This is one of his special characteristics, may God bless him and grant him peace, which no one else shares with him. There is no authentic hadith about the reward for deeds for anyone other than him in which he is forgiven his past and future sins. This is a great honor for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in all his affairs obedient, righteous, and upright, which no human being other than him has attained, neither from the first nor from the last. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the most perfect of all human beings and their master in this world and the hereafter. And since he was the most obedient of God’s creation to God and the most reverent of His commands and prohibitions, he said when the she-camel knelt before him: He who held back the elephant held her back. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they will not ask Me for anything today by which they glorify the sacred things of God except that I will respond to it. So when he obeyed God in that and responded to the peace, God, the Almighty, said to him: Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory * That God may forgive you your past and future sins and complete His favor. Upon you” meaning in this world and the hereafter and guides you to a straight path meaning by what He legislates for you of the great law and the upright religion and God will grant you a mighty victory meaning because of your submission to the command of God the Almighty, God will raise you up and grant you victory over your enemies as it came in the authentic hadith “And God does not increase a servant’s forgiveness except in honor. And no one humbles himself before God the Almighty except that God the Almighty will raise him up.” And on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: I have not punished anyone who disobeyed God the Almighty in you with anything like obeying God the Blessed and Exalted in him.

It was said to him: Has God not forgiven you your past and future sins? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Should I not be a grateful servant? They and the rest of the group narrated it, except for Abu Dawud, on the authority of Ziyad. Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Maruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Ibn Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed, he would stand until his feet would swell. Aisha may God be pleased with her said to him: O Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), do you do this when God has forgiven you your past and future sins? He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: O Aisha, should I not be a grateful servant? Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn Al-Husayn narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Awf Al-Kharraz - who was trustworthy in Makkah - Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Misa’ar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) stood until his feet - or he said his legs - swelled. It was said to him: Has God not forgiven you your past and future sins? He said: Should I not be a grateful servant? This is strange from this perspective. His saying: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest means clear and apparent. What is meant by it is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, because of it, abundant goodness occurred, people believed and gathered together, the believer spoke to the disbeliever, and beneficial knowledge and faith spread. And the Almighty’s saying: So that God may forgive you your past and future sins. This is one of his special characteristics, may God bless him and grant him peace, which no one else shares with him. There is no authentic hadith about the reward for deeds for anyone other than him in which he is forgiven his past and future sins. This is a great honor for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in all his affairs obedient, righteous, and upright, which no human being other than him has attained, neither from the first nor from the last. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the most perfect of all human beings and their master in this world and the hereafter. And since he was the most obedient of God’s creation to God and the most reverent of His commands and prohibitions, he said when the she-camel knelt before him: He who held back the elephant held her back. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they will not ask Me for anything today by which they glorify the sacred things of God except that I will respond to it. So when he obeyed God in that and responded to the peace, God, the Almighty, said to him: Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory * That God may forgive you your past and future sins and complete His favor. Upon you” meaning in this world and the hereafter and guides you to a straight path meaning by what He legislates for you of the great law and the upright religion and God will grant you a mighty victory meaning because of your submission to the command of God the Almighty, God will raise you up and grant you victory over your enemies as it came in the authentic hadith “And God does not increase a servant’s forgiveness except in honor. And no one humbles himself before God the Almighty except that God the Almighty will raise him up.” And on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: I have not punished anyone who disobeyed God the Almighty in you with anything like obeying God the Blessed and Exalted in him.
48:4: God the Almighty says: It is He who sent down tranquility meaning He made peace. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him and him, said: Mercy. Qatada said: Dignity in the hearts of the believers, who are the Companions, may God be pleased with them, on the day of Hudaybiyyah who responded to God and His Messenger and submitted to the judgment of God and His Messenger. When their hearts were reassured by that and settled, He increased their faith along with their faith. Al-Bukhari and other imams used it as evidence of the difference in faith in the hearts. Then God the Almighty mentioned that if He had willed, We would not have been victorious over the disbelievers, so He the Almighty said: And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth meaning if He had sent against them a single angel, He would have destroyed their greenery. However, God the Almighty has prescribed jihad and fighting for His believing servants, because of the profound wisdom, decisive proof, and overwhelming evidence in that. For this reason, He the Almighty said: And God is Knowing and Wise. Then God the Almighty said: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Anas may God be pleased with him had already said: Congratulations, O Messenger of God! This is for you, but what is for us? So God the Almighty revealed: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. That is, they will remain therein forever. And He will remove from them their misdeeds. That is, their sins and transgressions. He will not punish them for them, but will pardon, overlook, forgive, conceal, have mercy, and be grateful. And that is in the sight of God a great attainment. Like His saying, the Almighty: So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. God the Almighty says: And He punishes the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women who think ill of God. That is, they accuse God the Almighty of His judgment and think that the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, may God be pleased with them, will be killed and gone completely. For this reason, God the Almighty says: Upon them is a cycle of evil, and the wrath and the curse of God are upon them, that is, He distanced them from His mercy, and prepared for them Hell, and evil it is as a destination. Then the Almighty says, confirming His ability to take revenge on the enemies, the enemies of Islam, and on the infidels and hypocrites, And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
