48:8: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness meaning over creation and a bringer of good tidings meaning to the believers and a warner meaning to the disbelievers. Its explanation has been presented previously in Surat Al-Ahzab. That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and others said: To glorify and honor him from tawqir which is respect, veneration, and reverence and to exalt Him meaning to exalt God morning and evening meaning at the beginning and end of the day. Then the Almighty said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to honor, glorify, and glorify him: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God, as He, the Most High, says: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. “The hand of God is over their hands,” meaning He is present with them, hearing their words, seeing their place, and knowing their inner and outer aspects. He, the Most High, is the one who is pledged allegiance to through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He, the Most High, says: “Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Fadl bin Yahya Al-Anbari told us, Ali bin Bakkar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever draws his sword in the way of God has pledged allegiance to God. My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Mughirah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about al-Hijr 15:“By God, God Almighty will raise it up on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which to see and a tongue with which to speak, and it will bear witness against whoever touches it with truth. So whoever touches it has pledged allegiance to God Almighty.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God. The Hand of God is over their hands.” That is why God Almighty said here: But whoever breaks his pledge, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. That is, the consequences of that will only come back to the breaker, and God is independent of him. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God - He will give him a great reward. Great” meaning a great reward. This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, and it took place under a samr tree in Al-Hudaibiyah. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day were said to be one thousand three hundred, and it was said four hundred, and it was said five hundred, and the middle is more correct. Mentioning the hadiths mentioned in this regard Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: On the day of Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission, and they both also included it on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Abu Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: On that day we were one thousand four hundred. He placed his hand in the water and the water started gushing out from between his fingers until they were all satisfied. This is an abbreviation from another context when he mentioned the story of their thirst on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave them an arrow from his quiver and they put it in the well of Hudaybiyyah, and it gushes forth with water until it sufficed them. It was said to Jabir may God be pleased with him: How many were you on that day? He said: We were one thousand four hundred. If we had been one hundred thousand, it would have been enough for us. In a narration in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him they say they were fifteen hundred. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Qatada: I said to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: Fifteen hundred. I said: Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, said they were fourteen hundred. He, may God have mercy on him, said: They are mistaken. He told me that they were fifteen hundred. Al-Bayhaqi said: This narration indicates that in the past he used to say fifteen hundred, then he mentioned the mistake and said fourteen hundred. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. The well-known narration that was narrated by more than one person from him is fourteen hundred. This is what Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Al-Hakim from Al-Asamm from Al-Abbas Al-Duri from Yahya ibn Ma’in from Shababah ibn Suwar from Shu’bah from Qatadah from Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab from his father who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree one thousand four hundred. This is also what is in the narration of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa’, Mu’qil ibn Yasar, and Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, may God be pleased with them. More than one of the authors of the campaigns and biographies say this. The two authors of the Sahih narrated from the hadith of Shu’bah from Amr ibn Murrah who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, may God be pleased with him, say: The companions of the tree were one thousand four hundred. Aslam was at that time the eighth of the emigrants. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in his Seerah on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr on the authority of Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn Al-Hakam that they told him: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, each sacrificial animal for ten people. Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with them both, according to what I heard from him, said: We at Al-Hudaybiyah were fourteen hundred. This is what Ibn Ishaq said, and it is considered one of his delusions, as what is preserved in the two Sahihs is that they were several hundred, as will come later, God willing. Mention the reason for this great pledge Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in Al-Seerah: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, to send him to Mecca, to inform the nobles of Quraysh of what he had come to him with. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from Quraysh, and there is no one in Mecca from the Banu Adi bin Kaab to protect me. Quraysh knows of my enmity towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will direct you to a man who is more honored among them than I am, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him. We will send him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he did not come to fight, but rather he came to visit this House and to respect its sanctity. Uthman may God be pleased with him set out for Mecca. Abaan ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Mecca, or before he did so. He carried him in his arms and gave him protection until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Uthman may God be pleased with him set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh and conveyed to them what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had sent him with. When Uthman may God be pleased with him finished delivering the message of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to them, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then do so. He said: "I would not do that until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) circumambulates it." Quraysh detained him with them. report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims that Uthman may God be pleased with him had been killed. Ibn Ishaq said: "Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that Uthman had been killed, he said: 'We will not leave until we fight the people.'" The Messenger of God called the people to the pledge of allegiance, and it was the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree. The people were saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged them to die. Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, was saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pledge them to die, but he pledged us not to flee. So the people pledged allegiance, and none of the Muslims who were present remained behind except Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Banu Salamah. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, was saying: By God, it is as if I see him clinging to the armpit of his camel, leaning towards it to hide from the people. Then it came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what happened with Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was false. Ibn Lahi’ah mentioned on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, something similar to this context, and he added to his context that the Quraysh sent, while Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was with them, Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd Al-Uzza, and Mukraz ibn Hafs to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. While they were with them, a conversation took place between some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, and they threw arrows and stones at each other, and the two groups shouted: Both of them pledged allegiance to the messengers they had with them. The herald of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called out: “Behold, the Holy Spirit has descended upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and has commanded the pledge of allegiance, so go out in the name of God the Most High and pledge allegiance.” The Muslims went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was under the tree and pledged allegiance to him that they would never flee. This terrified the polytheists and they sent whoever was with them of the Muslims and called for truce and peace. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdun told us, Ahmad bin Ubaid Al-Saffar told us, Hisham told us, Al-Hasan bin Bishr told us, Al-Hakam bin Abdul-Malik told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the Pledge of Ridwan, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of Mecca. So the people pledged allegiance, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, Uthman is in need of God Almighty and the need of His Messenger. So he clapped one of his hands against the other, and the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was better for Uthman, may God be pleased with him, than their hands for themselves. Ibn Hisham said: “Someone I trust told me, on the authority of someone who told him with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Abu Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both, who said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pledged allegiance to Uthman may God be pleased with him, and he clapped one hand against the other.’” Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham al-Nahwi said: “Then Wakee’ mentioned on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘The first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the Pledge of Ridwan was Abu Sinan al-Asadi.’” Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaidi said: “Sufyan told us, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called the people to the pledge of allegiance, the first one to go to him was Abu Sinan al-Asadi, and he said: ‘Extend your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘On what are you pledging allegiance to me?’ Abu Sinan may God be pleased with him said: ‘On what is in your heart.’” This is Abu Sinan Wahb al-Asadi may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari said: Shuja’ ibn al-Walid told us that he heard al-Nadr ibn Muhammad say: Sakhr told us on the authority of Nafi’ may God be pleased with him who said: People say that Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both embraced Islam before Umar, but that is not the case. Rather, on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, Umar may God be pleased with him sent Abdullah to a horse of his that was with a man from the Ansar, to bring it to him to fight on while the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was pledging allegiance under the tree, and Umar may God be pleased with him did not know about that. Abdullah may God be pleased with him pledged allegiance to him, then he went to the horse and brought it to Umar may God be pleased with him, while Umar may God be pleased with him was seeking permission to fight. He informed him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was pledging allegiance under the tree, so he set off and went with him until he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). This is what people say: that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar may God be pleased with them both. Then Al-Bukhari said, and Hisham bin Ammar said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Umar bin Muhammad Al-Amri told us, Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The people were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had dispersed in the shade of the trees. Then they surrounded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, meaning Umar, may God be pleased with him: O servant of God, see what is the matter with the people who have surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He found them pledging allegiance, so he pledged allegiance. Then he returned to Umar, may God be pleased with him, and he went out and pledged allegiance. Al-Bayhaqi has attributed it to Abu Amr Al-Adeeb, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Sufyan, on the authority of Duhaim. Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, and he mentioned it. Al-Layth said, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were 1,400 on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and we pledged allegiance to him. Umar, may God be pleased with him, took him by the hand under the tree, which was a tamarisk tree, and said: We pledge allegiance to him on the condition that we do not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. Narrated by Muslim, on the authority of Qutaybah, on his authority. Muslim narrated on the authority of Yahya ibn Yahya, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abdullah Al-A’raj, on the authority of Ma’qil ibn Yasar may God be pleased with him, who said: “I saw myself on the Day of the Tree while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was giving the people their pledge of allegiance, and I was raising one of its branches above his head, and we were fourteen hundred.” He said: We did not give him the pledge of allegiance to die, but we gave him the pledge not to flee. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid, on the authority of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa’ may God be pleased with him, who said: “I gave the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) under the tree.” Yazid said: “I said: ‘O Abu Maslama, on what were you giving your pledge of allegiance that day?’ He said: ‘On death.’” Al-Bukhari also said: Abu Asim told us! Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid told us, on the authority of Salamah may God be pleased with him, who said: “I gave the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, then I stepped aside, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Salamah, will you not give the pledge of allegiance?” I said: I have already given the pledge. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Come forward and give the pledge of allegiance. So I approached him and pledged allegiance to him. I said: What did you pledge allegiance to him for, O Salamah? He said: For death. Muslim narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid, and Al-Bukhari narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibad ibn Tamim that they pledged allegiance to him for death. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ahmad ibn Salamah informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abu Amir al-Aqdi informed us, Abdul-Malik ibn Amr informed us, Akrima ibn Ammar al-Yamami informed us, on the authority of Iyas ibn Salamah, on the authority of his father Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, may God be pleased with him, who said: We arrived at al-Hudaybiyah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were fourteen hundred, and there were fifty sheep on them that could not satisfy their thirst. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on a well, meaning the basin, and either supplicated or spat into it, and it spurted, so we drank and were watered. He said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for the pledge of allegiance at the base of the tree, and I was the first of the people to pledge allegiance to him. Then he pledged allegiance and pledged allegiance until he was in the middle of the people, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Pledge allegiance to me, O Salamah. I said: O Messenger of God, I pledged allegiance to you among the first of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And also. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw me unarmed and gave me a shield or a shield, then he pledged allegiance until he was at the end of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Will you not pledge allegiance, O Salamah? I said: O Messenger of God, I pledged allegiance to you among the first and middle of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And also. So I pledged allegiance to him a third time, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Salamah, where is your shield or your shield that I gave you? I said: O Messenger of God, ‘Amir met me unarmed and I gave it to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and then said: You are like the one who said the first, ‘O God, make me a beloved one who is more beloved to me than myself.’ He said: Then the polytheists of Makkah sent us messages about peace until some of us walked among the others and we reconciled. He said: I was a servant of Talha ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, I used to water his horse, groom it and eat from his food, and I left my family and wealth, emigrating to God and His Messenger. When we and the people of Makkah made peace and some of us mingled with each other, I went to a tree and cut its thorns, then I lay down at its base in its shade. Four polytheists of Makkah came to me and started attacking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I hated them and moved to another tree, so they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, a caller called from the bottom of the valley: O emigrants, Ibn Zanim has been killed! So I drew my sword and attacked those four while they were asleep. I took their weapons and put them in a bunch in my hand and said: By the One Who honored the face of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), none of you will raise his head except that I will strike the one in which his eyes are! He said: Then I brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: My uncle Amir brought a man from the Ublat tribe called Makraz, one of the polytheists, leading him until we stopped with them before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with seventy polytheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at them and said: Leave them alone, for they will be the ones who started the immorality and then turned back. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgave them, and God, the Almighty, revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them (al-An`am 4:17). Muslim narrated it in this way on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Rahawayh with a chain of transmission similar to it or close to it. It was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu ‘Awanah, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree. He said: We set out the next year on pilgrimage and its location was hidden from us. If it has become clear to you, then you know best. Abu Bakr al-Humaidi said: Sufyan told us, Abu al-Zubayr told us, Jabir, may God be pleased with him, told us, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people to the pledge of allegiance, we found a man from among us called al-Jadd ibn Qays hiding under the armpit of his camel. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr with it. Al-Hamidi also said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr that he heard Jabir, may God be pleased with him, say: We were on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, fourteen hundred, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: You are the best people on earth today. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: If I had been more discerning, I would have shown you the location of the tree. Sufyan said that they differed about its location. They both included it from the hadith of Sufyan. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas al-Mukhrami narrated to us, Saeed ibn Amr al-Ash'athi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Abdi narrated to us, on the authority of Khidash ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever pledges allegiance under the tree will all enter Paradise except the owner of the red camel. He said: "So we set out to hasten to him, and there was a man who had lost his camel, so we said: Come and pledge allegiance. He said: My camel being lost is dearer to me than my pledging allegiance." Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us, on the authority of my father, on the authority of Qurrah, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever ascends the pass, Thaniyat al-Marar, will have his sins forgiven as were committed against the Children of Israel. The first to ascend the cavalry of Banu Khazraj, then the people rushed to him after that, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of you will be forgiven except the owner of the red camel. We said: Come, so that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may ask forgiveness for you. He said: By God, finding what I lost would be more beloved to me than for your companion to seek forgiveness for me. Then he was a man searching for something lost. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Ubayd God. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir may God be pleased with him say: Umm Mubashir told me that she heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say in the presence of Hafsah may God be pleased with her: None of the people of the tree who pledged allegiance under it will enter Hell, God willing. She said: Yes, O Messenger of God. So he rebuked her. Hafsah may God be pleased with her said: There is not one of you but will pass over it. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God Almighty has said: ‘Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.’” Narrated by Muslim. It also includes a narration on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him who said: A slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah came complaining about Hatib and said: O Messenger of God, Hatib will surely enter Hell. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have lied; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah. For this reason, God Almighty said in praise of them: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to God. The hand of God is over their hands. So whoever breaks his oath, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God…” Then He will give him a great reward,” as God Almighty said in another verse: “God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.”
48:9: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness meaning over creation and a bringer of good tidings meaning to the believers and a warner meaning to the disbelievers. Its explanation has been presented previously in Surat Al-Ahzab. That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and others said: To glorify and honor him from tawqir which is respect, veneration, and reverence and to exalt Him meaning to exalt God morning and evening meaning at the beginning and end of the day. Then the Almighty said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to honor, glorify, and glorify him: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God, as He, the Most High, says: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. “The hand of God is over their hands,” meaning He is present with them, hearing their words, seeing their place, and knowing their inner and outer aspects. He, the Most High, is the one who is pledged allegiance to through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He, the Most High, says: “Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Fadl bin Yahya Al-Anbari told us, Ali bin Bakkar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever draws his sword in the way of God has pledged allegiance to God. My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Mughirah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about al-Hijr 15:“By God, God Almighty will raise it up on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which to see and a tongue with which to speak, and it will bear witness against whoever touches it with truth. So whoever touches it has pledged allegiance to God Almighty.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God. The Hand of God is over their hands.” That is why God Almighty said here: But whoever breaks his pledge, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. That is, the consequences of that will only come back to the breaker, and God is independent of him. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God - He will give him a great reward. Great” meaning a great reward. This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, and it took place under a samr tree in Al-Hudaibiyah. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day were said to be one thousand three hundred, and it was said four hundred, and it was said five hundred, and the middle is more correct. Mentioning the hadiths mentioned in this regard Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: On the day of Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission, and they both also included it on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Abu Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: On that day we were one thousand four hundred. He placed his hand in the water and the water started gushing out from between his fingers until they were all satisfied. This is an abbreviation from another context when he mentioned the story of their thirst on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave them an arrow from his quiver and they put it in the well of Hudaybiyyah, and it gushes forth with water until it sufficed them. It was said to Jabir may God be pleased with him: How many were you on that day? He said: We were one thousand four hundred. If we had been one hundred thousand, it would have been enough for us. In a narration in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him they say they were fifteen hundred. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Qatada: I said to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: Fifteen hundred. I said: Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, said they were fourteen hundred. He, may God have mercy on him, said: They are mistaken. He told me that they were fifteen hundred. Al-Bayhaqi said: This narration indicates that in the past he used to say fifteen hundred, then he mentioned the mistake and said fourteen hundred. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. The well-known narration that was narrated by more than one person from him is fourteen hundred. This is what Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Al-Hakim from Al-Asamm from Al-Abbas Al-Duri from Yahya ibn Ma’in from Shababah ibn Suwar from Shu’bah from Qatadah from Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab from his father who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree one thousand four hundred. This is also what is in the narration of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa’, Mu’qil ibn Yasar, and Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, may God be pleased with them. More than one of the authors of the campaigns and biographies say this. The two authors of the Sahih narrated from the hadith of Shu’bah from Amr ibn Murrah who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, may God be pleased with him, say: The companions of the tree were one thousand four hundred. Aslam was at that time the eighth of the emigrants. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in his Seerah on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr on the authority of Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn Al-Hakam that they told him: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, each sacrificial animal for ten people. Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with them both, according to what I heard from him, said: We at Al-Hudaybiyah were fourteen hundred. This is what Ibn Ishaq said, and it is considered one of his delusions, as what is preserved in the two Sahihs is that they were several hundred, as will come later, God willing. Mention the reason for this great pledge Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in Al-Seerah: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, to send him to Mecca, to inform the nobles of Quraysh of what he had come to him with. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from Quraysh, and there is no one in Mecca from the Banu Adi bin Kaab to protect me. Quraysh knows of my enmity towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will direct you to a man who is more honored among them than I am, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him. We will send him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he did not come to fight, but rather he came to visit this House and to respect its sanctity. Uthman may God be pleased with him set out for Mecca. Abaan ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Mecca, or before he did so. He carried him in his arms and gave him protection until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Uthman may God be pleased with him set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh and conveyed to them what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had sent him with. When Uthman may God be pleased with him finished delivering the message of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to them, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then do so. He said: "I would not do that until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) circumambulates it." Quraysh detained him with them. report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims that Uthman may God be pleased with him had been killed. Ibn Ishaq said: "Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that Uthman had been killed, he said: 'We will not leave until we fight the people.'" The Messenger of God called the people to the pledge of allegiance, and it was the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree. The people were saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged them to die. Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, was saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pledge them to die, but he pledged us not to flee. So the people pledged allegiance, and none of the Muslims who were present remained behind except Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Banu Salamah. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, was saying: By God, it is as if I see him clinging to the armpit of his camel, leaning towards it to hide from the people. Then it came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what happened with Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was false. Ibn Lahi’ah mentioned on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, something similar to this context, and he added to his context that the Quraysh sent, while Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was with them, Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd Al-Uzza, and Mukraz ibn Hafs to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. While they were with them, a conversation took place between some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, and they threw arrows and stones at each other, and the two groups shouted: Both of them pledged allegiance to the messengers they had with them. The herald of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called out: “Behold, the Holy Spirit has descended upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and has commanded the pledge of allegiance, so go out in the name of God the Most High and pledge allegiance.” The Muslims went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was under the tree and pledged allegiance to him that they would never flee. This terrified the polytheists and they sent whoever was with them of the Muslims and called for truce and peace. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdun told us, Ahmad bin Ubaid Al-Saffar told us, Hisham told us, Al-Hasan bin Bishr told us, Al-Hakam bin Abdul-Malik told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the Pledge of Ridwan, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of Mecca. So the people pledged allegiance, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, Uthman is in need of God Almighty and the need of His Messenger. So he clapped one of his hands against the other, and the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was better for Uthman, may God be pleased with him, than their hands for themselves. Ibn Hisham said: “Someone I trust told me, on the authority of someone who told him with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Abu Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both, who said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pledged allegiance to Uthman may God be pleased with him, and he clapped one hand against the other.’” Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham al-Nahwi said: “Then Wakee’ mentioned on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘The first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the Pledge of Ridwan was Abu Sinan al-Asadi.’” Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaidi said: “Sufyan told us, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called the people to the pledge of allegiance, the first one to go to him was Abu Sinan al-Asadi, and he said: ‘Extend your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘On what are you pledging allegiance to me?’ Abu Sinan may God be pleased with him said: ‘On what is in your heart.’” This is Abu Sinan Wahb al-Asadi may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari said: Shuja’ ibn al-Walid told us that he heard al-Nadr ibn Muhammad say: Sakhr told us on the authority of Nafi’ may God be pleased with him who said: People say that Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both embraced Islam before Umar, but that is not the case. Rather, on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, Umar may God be pleased with him sent Abdullah to a horse of his that was with a man from the Ansar, to bring it to him to fight on while the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was pledging allegiance under the tree, and Umar may God be pleased with him did not know about that. Abdullah may God be pleased with him pledged allegiance to him, then he went to the horse and brought it to Umar may God be pleased with him, while Umar may God be pleased with him was seeking permission to fight. He informed him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was pledging allegiance under the tree, so he set off and went with him until he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). This is what people say: that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar may God be pleased with them both. Then Al-Bukhari said, and Hisham bin Ammar said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Umar bin Muhammad Al-Amri told us, Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The people were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had dispersed in the shade of the trees. Then they surrounded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, meaning Umar, may God be pleased with him: O servant of God, see what is the matter with the people who have surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He found them pledging allegiance, so he pledged allegiance. Then he returned to Umar, may God be pleased with him, and he went out and pledged allegiance. Al-Bayhaqi has attributed it to Abu Amr Al-Adeeb, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Sufyan, on the authority of Duhaim. Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, and he mentioned it. Al-Layth said, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were 1,400 on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and we pledged allegiance to him. Umar, may God be pleased with him, took him by the hand under the tree, which was a tamarisk tree, and said: We pledge allegiance to him on the condition that we do not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. Narrated by Muslim, on the authority of Qutaybah, on his authority. Muslim narrated on the authority of Yahya ibn Yahya, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abdullah Al-A’raj, on the authority of Ma’qil ibn Yasar may God be pleased with him, who said: “I saw myself on the Day of the Tree while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was giving the people their pledge of allegiance, and I was raising one of its branches above his head, and we were fourteen hundred.” He said: We did not give him the pledge of allegiance to die, but we gave him the pledge not to flee. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid, on the authority of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa’ may God be pleased with him, who said: “I gave the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) under the tree.” Yazid said: “I said: ‘O Abu Maslama, on what were you giving your pledge of allegiance that day?’ He said: ‘On death.’” Al-Bukhari also said: Abu Asim told us! Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid told us, on the authority of Salamah may God be pleased with him, who said: “I gave the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, then I stepped aside, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Salamah, will you not give the pledge of allegiance?” I said: I have already given the pledge. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Come forward and give the pledge of allegiance. So I approached him and pledged allegiance to him. I said: What did you pledge allegiance to him for, O Salamah? He said: For death. Muslim narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid, and Al-Bukhari narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibad ibn Tamim that they pledged allegiance to him for death. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ahmad ibn Salamah informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abu Amir al-Aqdi informed us, Abdul-Malik ibn Amr informed us, Akrima ibn Ammar al-Yamami informed us, on the authority of Iyas ibn Salamah, on the authority of his father Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, may God be pleased with him, who said: We arrived at al-Hudaybiyah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were fourteen hundred, and there were fifty sheep on them that could not satisfy their thirst. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on a well, meaning the basin, and either supplicated or spat into it, and it spurted, so we drank and were watered. He said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for the pledge of allegiance at the base of the tree, and I was the first of the people to pledge allegiance to him. Then he pledged allegiance and pledged allegiance until he was in the middle of the people, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Pledge allegiance to me, O Salamah. I said: O Messenger of God, I pledged allegiance to you among the first of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And also. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw me unarmed and gave me a shield or a shield, then he pledged allegiance until he was at the end of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Will you not pledge allegiance, O Salamah? I said: O Messenger of God, I pledged allegiance to you among the first and middle of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And also. So I pledged allegiance to him a third time, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Salamah, where is your shield or your shield that I gave you? I said: O Messenger of God, ‘Amir met me unarmed and I gave it to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and then said: You are like the one who said the first, ‘O God, make me a beloved one who is more beloved to me than myself.’ He said: Then the polytheists of Makkah sent us messages about peace until some of us walked among the others and we reconciled. He said: I was a servant of Talha ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, I used to water his horse, groom it and eat from his food, and I left my family and wealth, emigrating to God and His Messenger. When we and the people of Makkah made peace and some of us mingled with each other, I went to a tree and cut its thorns, then I lay down at its base in its shade. Four polytheists of Makkah came to me and started attacking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I hated them and moved to another tree, so they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, a caller called from the bottom of the valley: O emigrants, Ibn Zanim has been killed! So I drew my sword and attacked those four while they were asleep. I took their weapons and put them in a bunch in my hand and said: By the One Who honored the face of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), none of you will raise his head except that I will strike the one in which his eyes are! He said: Then I brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: My uncle Amir brought a man from the Ublat tribe called Makraz, one of the polytheists, leading him until we stopped with them before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with seventy polytheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at them and said: Leave them alone, for they will be the ones who started the immorality and then turned back. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgave them, and God, the Almighty, revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them (al-An`am 4:17). Muslim narrated it in this way on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Rahawayh with a chain of transmission similar to it or close to it. It was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu ‘Awanah, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree. He said: We set out the next year on pilgrimage and its location was hidden from us. If it has become clear to you, then you know best. Abu Bakr al-Humaidi said: Sufyan told us, Abu al-Zubayr told us, Jabir, may God be pleased with him, told us, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people to the pledge of allegiance, we found a man from among us called al-Jadd ibn Qays hiding under the armpit of his camel. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr with it. Al-Hamidi also said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr that he heard Jabir, may God be pleased with him, say: We were on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, fourteen hundred, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: You are the best people on earth today. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: If I had been more discerning, I would have shown you the location of the tree. Sufyan said that they differed about its location. They both included it from the hadith of Sufyan. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas al-Mukhrami narrated to us, Saeed ibn Amr al-Ash'athi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Abdi narrated to us, on the authority of Khidash ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever pledges allegiance under the tree will all enter Paradise except the owner of the red camel. He said: "So we set out to hasten to him, and there was a man who had lost his camel, so we said: Come and pledge allegiance. He said: My camel being lost is dearer to me than my pledging allegiance." Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us, on the authority of my father, on the authority of Qurrah, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever ascends the pass, Thaniyat al-Marar, will have his sins forgiven as were committed against the Children of Israel. The first to ascend the cavalry of Banu Khazraj, then the people rushed to him after that, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of you will be forgiven except the owner of the red camel. We said: Come, so that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may ask forgiveness for you. He said: By God, finding what I lost would be more beloved to me than for your companion to seek forgiveness for me. Then he was a man searching for something lost. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Ubayd God. Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir may God be pleased with him say: Umm Mubashir told me that she heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say in the presence of Hafsah may God be pleased with her: None of the people of the tree who pledged allegiance under it will enter Hell, God willing. She said: Yes, O Messenger of God. So he rebuked her. Hafsah may God be pleased with her said: There is not one of you but will pass over it. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God Almighty has said: ‘Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.’” Narrated by Muslim. It also includes a narration on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him who said: A slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah came complaining about Hatib and said: O Messenger of God, Hatib will surely enter Hell. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have lied; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah. For this reason, God Almighty said in praise of them: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to God. The hand of God is over their hands. So whoever breaks his oath, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God…” Then He will give him a great reward,” as God Almighty said in another verse: “God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.”
48:10: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness meaning over creation and a bringer of good tidings meaning to the believers and a warner meaning to the disbelievers. Its explanation has been presented previously in Surat Al-Ahzab. That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and others said: To glorify and honor him from tawqir which is respect, veneration, and reverence and to exalt Him meaning to exalt God morning and evening meaning at the beginning and end of the day. Then the Almighty said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to honor, glorify, and glorify him: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God, as He, the Most High, says: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. “The hand of God is over their hands,” meaning He is present with them, hearing their words, seeing their place, and knowing their inner and outer aspects. He, the Most High, is the one who is pledged allegiance to through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He, the Most High, says: “Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur’an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is what is the great attainment.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Fadl bin Yahya Al-Anbari told us, Ali bin Bakkar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever draws his sword in the way of God has pledged allegiance to God. My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Mughirah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about al-Hijr 15:“By God, God Almighty will raise it up on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes with which to see and a tongue with which to speak, and it will bear witness against whoever touches it with truth. So whoever touches it has pledged allegiance to God Almighty.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God. The Hand of God is over their hands.” That is why God Almighty said here: But whoever breaks his pledge, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. That is, the consequences of that will only come back to the breaker, and God is independent of him. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God - He will give him a great reward. Great” meaning a great reward. This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, and it took place under a samr tree in Al-Hudaibiyah. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day were said to be one thousand three hundred, and it was said four hundred, and it was said five hundred, and the middle is more correct. Mentioning the hadiths mentioned in this regard Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: On the day of Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission, and they both also included it on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Abu Jabir may God be pleased with him, who said: On that day we were one thousand four hundred. He placed his hand in the water and the water started gushing out from between his fingers until they were all satisfied. This is an abbreviation from another context when he mentioned the story of their thirst on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave them an arrow from his quiver and they put it in the well of Hudaybiyyah, and it gushes forth with water until it sufficed them. It was said to Jabir may God be pleased with him: How many were you on that day? He said: We were one thousand four hundred. If we had been one hundred thousand, it would have been enough for us. In a narration in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him they say they were fifteen hundred. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Qatada: I said to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: Fifteen hundred. I said: Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, said they were fourteen hundred. He, may God have mercy on him, said: They are mistaken. He told me that they were fifteen hundred. Al-Bayhaqi said: This narration indicates that in the past he used to say fifteen hundred, then he mentioned the mistake and said fourteen hundred. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. The well-known narration that was narrated by more than one person from him is fourteen hundred. This is what Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Al-Hakim from Al-Asamm from Al-Abbas Al-Duri from Yahya ibn Ma’in from Shababah ibn Suwar from Shu’bah from Qatadah from Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab from his father who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree one thousand four hundred. This is also what is in the narration of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa’, Mu’qil ibn Yasar, and Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, may God be pleased with them. More than one of the authors of the campaigns and biographies say this. The two authors of the Sahih narrated from the hadith of Shu’bah from Amr ibn Murrah who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, may God be pleased with him, say: The companions of the tree were one thousand four hundred. Aslam was at that time the eighth of the emigrants. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in his Seerah on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr on the authority of Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn Al-Hakam that they told him: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, each sacrificial animal for ten people. Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with them both, according to what I heard from him, said: We at Al-Hudaybiyah were fourteen hundred. This is what Ibn Ishaq said, and it is considered one of his delusions, as what is preserved in the two Sahihs is that they were several hundred, as will come later, God willing. Mention the reason for this great pledge Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in Al-Seerah: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, to send him to Mecca, to inform the nobles of Quraysh of what he had come to him with. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from Quraysh, and there is no one in Mecca from the Banu Adi bin Kaab to protect me. Quraysh knows of my enmity towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will direct you to a man who is more honored among them than I am, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him. We will send him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he did not come to fight, but rather he came to visit this House and to respect its sanctity. Uthman may God be pleased with him set out for Mecca. Abaan ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Mecca, or before he did so. He carried him in his arms and gave him protection until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Uthman may God be pleased with him set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh and conveyed to them what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had sent him with. When Uthman may God be pleased with him finished delivering the message of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to them, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then do so. He said: "I would not do that until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) circumambulates it." Quraysh detained him with them. report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims that Uthman may God be pleased with him had been killed. Ibn Ishaq said: "Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard that Uthman had been killed, he said: 'We will not leave until we fight the people.'" The Messenger of God called the people to the pledge of allegiance, and it was the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree. The people were saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged them to die. Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, was saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pledge them to die, but he pledged us not to flee. So the people pledged allegiance, and none of the Muslims who were present remained behind except Al-Jadd ibn Qays, the brother of Banu Salamah. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, was saying: By God, it is as if I see him clinging to the armpit of his camel, leaning towards it to hide from the people. Then it came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what happened with Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was false. Ibn Lahi’ah mentioned on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, something similar to this context, and he added to his context that the Quraysh sent, while Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was with them, Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd Al-Uzza, and Mukraz ibn Hafs to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. While they were with them, a conversation took place between some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, and they threw arrows and stones at each other, and the two groups shouted: Both of them pledged allegiance to the messengers they had with them. The herald of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called out: “Behold, the Holy Spirit has descended upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and has commanded the pledge of allegiance, so go out in the name of God the Most High and pledge allegiance.” The Muslims went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was under the tree and pledged allegiance to him that they would never flee. This terrified the polytheists and they sent whoever was with them of the Muslims and called for truce and peace. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdun told us, Ahmad bin Ubaid Al-Saffar told us, Hisham told us, Al-Hasan bin Bishr told us, Al-Hakam bin Abdul-Malik told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the Pledge of Ridwan, Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of Mecca. So the people pledged allegiance, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, Uthman is in need of God Almighty and the need of His Messenger. So he clapped one of his hands against the other, and the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was better for Uthman, may God be pleased with him, than their hands for themselves. Ibn Hisham said: “Someone I trust told me, on the authority of someone who told him with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Abu Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both, who said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pledged allegiance to Uthman may God be pleased with him, and he clapped one hand against the other.’” Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham al-Nahwi said: “Then Wakee’ mentioned on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘The first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the Pledge of Ridwan was Abu Sinan al-Asadi.’” Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaidi said: “Sufyan told us, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called the people to the pledge of allegiance, the first one to go to him was Abu Sinan al-Asadi, and he said: ‘Extend your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘On what are you pledging allegiance to me?’ Abu Sinan may God be pleased with him said: ‘On what is in your heart.’” This is Abu Sinan Wahb al-Asadi may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari said: Shuja’ ibn al-Walid told us that he heard al-Nadr ibn Muhammad say: Sakhr told us on the authority of Nafi’ may God be pleased with him who said: People say that Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both embraced Islam before Umar, but that is not the case. Rather, on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, Umar may God be pleased with him sent Abdullah to a horse of his that was with a man from the Ansar, to bring it to him to fight on while the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was pledging allegiance under the tree, and Umar may God be pleased with him did not know about that. Abdullah may God be pleased with him pledged allegiance to him, then he went to the horse and brought it to Umar may God be pleased with him, while Umar may God be pleased with him was seeking permission to fight. He informed him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was pledging allegiance under the tree, so he set off and went with him until he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). This is what people say: that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar may God be pleased with them both. Then Al-Bukhari said, and Hisham bin Ammar said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Umar bin Muhammad Al-Amri told us, Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The people were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had dispersed in the shade of the trees. Then they surrounded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, meaning Umar, may God be pleased with him: O servant of God, see what is the matter with the people who have surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He found them pledging allegiance, so he pledged allegiance. Then he returned to Umar, may God be pleased with him, and he went out and pledged allegiance. Al-Bayhaqi has attributed it to Abu Amr Al-Adeeb, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Sufyan, on the authority of Duhaim. Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, and he mentioned it. Al-Layth said, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were 1,400 on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and we pledged allegiance to him. Umar, may God be pleased with him, took him by the hand under the tree, which was a tamarisk tree, and said: We pledge allegiance to him on the condition that we do not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him to die. Narrated by Muslim, on the authority of Qutaybah, on his authority. Muslim narrated on the authority of Yahya ibn Yahya, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abdullah Al-A’raj, on the authority of Ma’qil ibn Yasar may God be pleased with him, who said: “I saw myself on the Day of the Tree while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was giving the people their pledge of allegiance, and I was raising one of its branches above his head, and we were fourteen hundred.” He said: We did not give him the pledge of allegiance to die, but we gave him the pledge not to flee. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid, on the authority of Salamah ibn Al-Akwa’ may God be pleased with him, who said: “I gave the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) under the tree.” Yazid said: “I said: ‘O Abu Maslama, on what were you giving your pledge of allegiance that day?’ He said: ‘On death.’” Al-Bukhari also said: Abu Asim told us! Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid told us, on the authority of Salamah may God be pleased with him, who said: “I gave the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the Day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, then I stepped aside, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O Salamah, will you not give the pledge of allegiance?” I said: I have already given the pledge. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Come forward and give the pledge of allegiance. So I approached him and pledged allegiance to him. I said: What did you pledge allegiance to him for, O Salamah? He said: For death. Muslim narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ubaid, and Al-Bukhari narrated it likewise on the authority of Ibad ibn Tamim that they pledged allegiance to him for death. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ahmad ibn Salamah informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abu Amir al-Aqdi informed us, Abdul-Malik ibn Amr informed us, Akrima ibn Ammar al-Yamami informed us, on the authority of Iyas ibn Salamah, on the authority of his father Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, may God be pleased with him, who said: We arrived at al-Hudaybiyah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were fourteen hundred, and there were fifty sheep on them that could not satisfy their thirst. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on a well, meaning the basin, and either supplicated or spat into it, and it spurted, so we drank and were watered. He said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for the pledge of allegiance at the base of the tree, and I was the first of the people to pledge allegiance to him. Then he pledged allegiance and pledged allegiance until he was in the middle of the people, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Pledge allegiance to me, O Salamah. I said: O Messenger of God, I pledged allegiance to you among the first of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And also. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw me unarmed and gave me a shield or a shield, then he pledged allegiance until he was at the end of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Will you not pledge allegiance, O Salamah? I said: O Messenger of God, I pledged allegiance to you among the first and middle of the people. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And also. So I pledged allegiance to him a third time, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Salamah, where is your shield or your shield that I gave you? I said: O Messenger of God, ‘Amir met me unarmed and I gave it to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and then said: You are like the one who said the first, ‘O God, make me a beloved one who is more beloved to me than myself.’ He said: Then the polytheists of Makkah sent us messages about peace until some of us walked among the others and we reconciled. He said: I was a servant of Talha ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, I used to water his horse, groom it and eat from his food, and I left my family and wealth, emigrating to God and His Messenger. When we and the people of Makkah made peace and some of us mingled with each other, I went to a tree and cut its thorns, then I lay down at its base in its shade. Four polytheists of Makkah came to me and started attacking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I hated them and moved to another tree, so they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, a caller called from the bottom of the valley: O emigrants, Ibn Zanim has been killed! So I drew my sword and attacked those four while they were asleep. I took their weapons and put them in a bunch in my hand and said: By the One Who honored the face of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), none of you will raise his head except that I will strike the one in which his eyes are! He said: Then I brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: My uncle Amir brought a man from the Ublat tribe called Makraz, one of the polytheists, leading him until we stopped with them before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with seventy polytheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at them and said: Leave them alone, for they will be the ones who started the immorality and then turned back. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgave them, and God, the Almighty, revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them (al-An`am 4:17). Muslim narrated it in this way on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Rahawayh with a chain of transmission similar to it or close to it. It was proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu ‘Awanah, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have lied; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah. For this reason, God Almighty said in praise of them: “Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to God. The hand of God is over their hands. So whoever breaks his oath, he only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God…” Then He will give him a great reward,” as God Almighty said in another verse: “God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest.”
48:11: God Almighty says, informing His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the excuses of the Bedouins who stayed behind, who chose to stay with their families and were busy, and left the journey with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They excused themselves by being busy for that reason, and asked that the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, seek forgiveness for them. This is a statement from them, not out of belief, but rather out of dissimulation and compromise. For this reason, God Almighty said: “They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, ‘Then who can control anything for you from God if He intends you harm or intends you benefit?’” That is, no one is able to ward off what God Almighty and Holy intends for you, and He is the All-Knowing of your secrets, even if you treat us with dissimulation and hypocrisy. For this reason, God Almighty said: Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do. Then God Almighty said: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, that is, your staying behind was not an excused or sinful stay, but rather a hypocritical stay. Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, that is, you believed that they They will be killed, their roots will be uprooted, their green lands will be destroyed, and no one will return from them to inform them. And you assumed an evil assumption and you were a people who were ruined, meaning destroyed. This was said by Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Mujahid, and more than one other person. Qatadah said: Corrupt, and it was also said that it is the language of Oman. Then God the Almighty made clear that He is the Ruler, the Owner, who controls the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning for whoever repents to Him, returns to Him, and submits to Him.

Mujahid, Qatadah, and Juwaybir said that this is the promise that He promised the people of Hudaybiyyah, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Say, ‘You will never follow us.’ Thus said God before, meaning God promised the people of Hudaybiyyah before you asked to go out with them.
