Rather, they did not understand except a little, meaning that the matter was not as they claimed, but they did not understand.
48:16: The commentators differed regarding these people whom they call to, who are men of great strength, with statements: One of them is that they are Hawazin, narrated by Shu'bah from Abu Bishr from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, or both of them, and Hisham narrated it from Abu Bishr from them both, and Qatadah says the same in a narration from him. The second is Thaqif, said Ad-Dahhak. The third is Banu Hanifa, said Juwaybir and narrated by Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Az-Zuhri, and a similar narration was narrated from Sa'id and Ikrimah. The fourth is the people of Persia, narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and this is what Ata', Mujahid, and Ikrimah say in one of the narrations from him. Ka'b Al-Ahbar said: They are the Romans. Ibn Abi Layla, Ata', Al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: They are the Persians and the Romans. Mujahid said: They are the people of idols. He also said: They are men of great strength, but he did not specify a group. Ibn Jurayj said the same, and it is the preferred view of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Ashja’ told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Qawariri told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding the Almighty’s statement: You will be called to a people of great strength, he said: Those have not yet come. And my father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God the Almighty: You will be called to fight a people of great might, he said: They are the prominent ones. He said: And Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Hour will not come until you fight a people with small eyes and flat noses, whose faces are like hammered shields. Sufyan said: They are the Turks. Ibn Abi Omar said: I found it in another place. Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, came down to us and explained the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Fight a people whose sandals are made of hair, he said: They are the prominent ones, meaning the Kurds. And the words of God the Almighty: You fight them or they submit, means that jihad and fighting against them has been prescribed for you, and that will continue against them, and you have victory over them or they submit and enter your religion without fighting, but by choice. Then God the Almighty said: {If you obey} meaning if you respond and go out for jihad and fulfill your duty in it, {God will give you a good reward. But if you turn away as you turned away before} meaning the time of Hudaybiyyah when you were called but stayed behind, {He will punish you with a painful punishment.} Then God the Almighty mentioned the excuses for abandoning jihad. Some of them are necessary, such as blindness and persistent lameness, and others are incidental, such as an illness that lasts for a few days and then goes away. While sick, a person is included among those who have necessary excuses until he recovers. Then God the Almighty said, encouraging people to engage in jihad and obey God and His Messenger: {And whoever obeys God and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever turns away} meaning if he refrains from jihad and focuses on earning a living, {He will punish him with a painful punishment} in this world with humiliation and in the Hereafter with the Fire. And God the Almighty knows best.

48:18: God the Almighty informs us of His pleasure with the believers who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) under the tree. 48:20: Mujahid said about the Almighty’s saying: God has promised you many spoils that you will take which are all the spoils up to this day. So He hastened this for you meaning the conquest of Khaybar. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, So He hastened this for you meaning the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah And He withheld the hands of people from you meaning that no harm would come to you because of what your enemies had planned for you in terms of fighting and fighting. Likewise, He withheld the hands of people from you whom you left behind, from your families and women. And that it may be a sign for the believers meaning that they may take heed from that, for God the Almighty has protected them and supported them against all other enemies despite their small number. And so that they may know by this action of God for them that He is All-Knowing of the consequences of things, and that what He chooses for His believing servants is good even if they dislike it on the surface, as God the Almighty said: And perhaps you dislike a thing which is good for you “And He guides you to a straight path” meaning because of your submission to His command, your following His obedience, and your agreement with Him. His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. God the Almighty said: {And another which you have not been able to obtain, God has encompassed it. And God is over all things competent.} That is, another spoil of war and another specific conquest which you were not able to obtain, which God has made easy for you and encompassed for you. Indeed, God provides for His righteous servants from where they do not expect. The commentators differed as to what is meant by this spoil of war. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both that it refers to Khaybar. This is based on the statement of God the Almighty: {And He has hastened this for you.} It refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The sacrificial offering was seventy camels, as will come, God willing. For this reason God the Almighty said: You did not know them, lest you trample them and a disgrace should befall you because of them meaning sin and penalty without knowledge, so that God may admit into His mercy whom He wills. That is, He delays their punishment in order to rid them of the believers, and for many of them to return to Islam. Then the Blessed and Exalted said: If you were to separate that is, if the disbelievers were to be distinguished from the believers among them, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment that is, We would have given you power over them, and you would have killed them in a terrible manner. I asked Abu Zur’ah about it, but he did not know it except from this source. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Abdullah bin Saleh narrated to us, Al-Layth narrated to me, Abdul Rahman bin Khalid narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, informed him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but God. Whoever says: There is no god but God, his wealth and his life are protected from me, except for his right, and his reckoning is with God Almighty.” And God revealed in His Book and mentioned a people, saying: “Indeed, when it was said to them: There is no god but God, they were arrogant.” And God Almighty said: His praise: And he made them adhere to the word of piety, and they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it. It is There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. But they were arrogant about it, and the polytheists were arrogant about it on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them regarding the term. Ibn Jarir narrated it with these additions from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, and it appears that it was inserted from the words of Al-Zuhri, and God knows best. Mujahid said: The word of piety is sincerity. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: It is: “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.” Yunus ibn Bakir said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. Ath-Thawri said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. Ibn Umar said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God, and God is Great. Ibn Umar said the same, may God be pleased with them both. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the words of God, And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: The testimony that there is no god but God, which is the head of all piety. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God and jihad in His cause. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: It is: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Muammar said: Ath-Thawri said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, saying: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Qatada said, And He made them adhere to the word of piety. He said, There is no god but God. “And they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it.” The Muslims were more deserving of it and more worthy of it. And God is Knowing of all things. That is, He knows who deserves good and who deserves evil. An-Nasa’i said: Ibrahim ibn Sa’id told us, Shababah ibn Suwar told us, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Ala’ ibn Nuwayr, on the authority of Bishr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, may God be pleased with him, that he used to recite, When those who disbelieved put into their hearts arrogance, the arrogance of the times of ignorance. And if you had been as arrogant as they were, the Sacred Mosque would have been ruined. report of that reached ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, so he spoke harshly to him and said, “You know that I used to go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would teach me from what God had taught him.” ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, said, Rather, you are a man who has knowledge and the Qur’an, so recite and learn from what God and His Messenger have taught you. This is a mention of the hadiths related to the story of Hudaybiyyah and the story of the peace treaty. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn Al-Hakam, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, so each sacrificial animal was for ten. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he was at Usfan, where Bishr ibn Sufyan Al-Ka’bi met him and said: O Messenger of God, these are the Quraysh. They heard of your march, so they went out with them, wearing tiger skins, and they pledged to God Almighty that they would never enter it upon them by force. And here is Khalid ibn Al-Walid with their cavalry, whom they have advanced to Kara’ Al-Ghamim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Woe to the Quraysh! War has consumed them. What would they suffer if they left me alone with the rest of the people? If they defeat me, then what they wanted will happen, and if God Almighty makes me victorious, they will enter Islam in great numbers, and if they do not, they will fight and have strength. So what do the Quraysh think? By God, I will not cease…” I will fight them for that with which God the Almighty has sent me until God the Almighty makes me victorious or this forerunner is left alone.” Then he ordered the people to take the right between the two sides of Al-Hamd on a road that leads out to the pass of Al-Marar and Al-Hudaybiyah from the bottom of Mecca. He said: So he took the army that road, and when the Quraysh cavalry saw that the army had deviated from their path, they galloped back to the Quraysh. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out until he took the pass of Al-Marar, and his she-camel knelt down and the people said: She has not lain down. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “She has not lain down and that is not her nature, but He who held back the elephant from Mecca held her back. By God, if the Quraysh call me today to a plan in which they ask me to maintain kinship ties, I will give it to them.” Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the people, Go down. They said, O Messenger of God, there is no water in this valley for people to go down to. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his companions. He went down into one of those wells and stuck it in it. Water gushed forth until the people drove away from it with sticks. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was at peace, there was Budayl ibn Warqa’ with some men from Khuza’ah. He said to them the same as he had said to Bishr ibn Sufyan. They returned to the Quraysh and said, “O people of Quraysh, you are hastening to punish Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Muhammad did not come to fight, he only came as a visitor to this House and to honor its rights.” So they accused them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Al-Zuhri said: Khuza’a was in the possession of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, both polytheists and Muslims, and they did not hide from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, anything that was in Mecca. They said: If he only came for that purpose, then by God he will never enter it against us by force, and the Arabs will not speak of that. Then they sent to him Mukraz ibn Hafs, one of the Banu Amir ibn Lu’ayy. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: This is a treacherous man. When he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, spoke to him in a manner similar to what he had spoken to his companions. Then he returned to Quraysh and informed them of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, had said to him. They sent to him Al-Hulays ibn Alqama Al-Kinani, who was at that time the chief of the Abyssinians. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: This is from a people who are godless, so send the sacrificial animals. When he saw the sacrificial animals flowing towards him from the width of the valley in their necklaces, their hair having been eaten away by the length of the detention from… His place, he returned and did not reach the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of respect for what he saw, so he said: O people of Quraysh, I have seen something that is not permissible to hang the sacrificial animals in its necklaces, its hair has eaten away from being kept in its place for a long time. They said: Sit down, you are only a Bedouin and you have no knowledge. So they sent to him Urwah ibn Mas`ud Al-Thaqafi who said: O people of Quraysh, I have seen what happens to those you send to Muhammad when he comes to you of abuse and bad language. You know that you are a father and I am a son. I heard about what happened to you, so I gathered those of my people who obeyed me and then came until I consoled you with myself. They said: You have spoken the truth. You are not accused in our eyes. So he went out until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and sat before him and said: O Muhammad, you have gathered the rabble of the people and then you have come to your house to destroy it. It is Quraysh who have come out with the most precious of incantations. They have put on the skins of tigers and pledged to God Almighty that you will never enter it upon them by force. By God, it is as if I see these people fleeing from you tomorrow. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was sitting behind the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: Suck the clitoris of Al-Lat, should we flee from it? He said: Who is this, O Muhammad? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is the son of Abu Quhafah. He said: By God, were it not for the favor you had upon me, I would have rewarded you with it, but for this. Then he grabbed the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah may God be pleased with him was standing over the head of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with iron. He struck his hand and said: “Retain your hand from the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before, by God, it does not reach you.” He said: Woe to you, how rude and coarse you are! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiled. He said: Who is this, O Muhammad? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is your nephew, Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah. He said: “He is treacherous. Did you wash your private parts until yesterday?” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke to him in the same way he had spoken to his companions, and informed him that he had not come intending war. He said: So he got up from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he saw what his companions were doing to him. He did not perform ablution without them rushing to him, nor did he spit without them rushing to him, nor did anything fall from his hair without them taking it. So he returned to the Quraysh and said: O people of Quraysh, I came to Khosrau in his kingdom, and I came to Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms, and by God I have never seen a king like Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his companions. I have seen people who would never surrender him for anything, so follow your opinion. He said: Before that, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had sent Khurash ibn Umayyah Al-Khuza’i to Mecca, and he carried him on his camel called Al-Thalab. When he entered Mecca, the Quraysh attacked him and wanted to kill Khurash, but the Abyssinians prevented them until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He called for Umar may God be pleased with him to send him to Mecca. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from the Quraysh, and there is no one from Banu Adi among them to protect me. The Quraysh know of my enmity towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will guide you to a man who is more honorable among them than I am: Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and sent him to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but had come to visit this House and to respect its sanctity. So Uthman, may God be pleased with him, set out until he reached Mecca, and he was met by Abaan ibn Sa`id ibn al-`As. He got down from his mount and carried him in front of him, made him ride behind him and protected him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman, may God be pleased with him, set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent him with. They said to Uthman, may God be pleased with him, If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: “I would not do that until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulates it.” He said: The Quraysh detained him with them. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Uthman, may God be pleased with him, had been killed. Muhammad said: Al-Zuhri told me that the Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn Amr and said: Go to Muhammad and make peace with him, and do not be lenient in your peace treaty unless he withdraws from us this year. By God, the Arabs will never say that he entered our country by force again. So Suhayl ibn Amr went to him, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: “The people wanted peace when they sent this man.” When he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they spoke at length and went back and forth until peace was concluded between them. When the matter was settled and nothing remained but the written document, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, jumped up and went to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and said: O Abu Bakr, is he not the Messenger of God? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists? He said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give in to contempt in our religion? Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Umar, stick to his planting wherever he is, for I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God. Omar may God be pleased with him said: And I bear witness. Then he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give in to humiliation in our religion? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I am the servant of God and His Messenger. I will not disobey His command and He will not let me down.” Then Omar may God be pleased with him said: I continued to fast, pray, give charity, and free slaves because of what I did, fearing what I said that day, until I hoped that it would be good. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and said: Write In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Suhayl said: I do not know this, but write: In Your name, O God. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Write in your name, O God. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed to.” Suhayl ibn Amr said to him: “If I testify that you are the Messenger of God, I would not fight you. But write: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah and Suhayl ibn Amr have agreed to, to cease war for ten years, during which people will be safe and will refrain from attacking one another. However, whoever of his companions comes to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, without the permission of his guardian, he will be returned to him. Whoever of those with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes to the Quraysh, they will not return him. There will be a closed bond between us and there will be no chains or shackles. Among their conditions when they wrote the document was that whoever wanted to enter into the contract and covenant of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he will enter into it, and whoever wanted to enter into the contract and covenant of the Quraysh, he will enter into it. Then Khuza’ah rose up and said: We are in the contract and covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Banu Bakr rose up and said: We are in the contract and covenant of the Quraysh. You will withdraw from us this year and not enter Mecca upon us. And when it is the next year, we will leave you and you will enter it with your companions.” I stayed there for three days, with the weapon of a rider. Do not enter it with anything but swords in their scabbards. While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was writing the document, Abu Jandal bin Suhayl bin Amr came to him in chains that had been stolen from him to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had gone out, and they had no doubt about the victory, due to a vision that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had seen. When they saw what they saw of the peace and the return, and what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had endured, the people were deeply troubled by that, until they were about to perish. When Suhayl saw Abu Jandal, he stood up and slapped him in the face. He said: O Muhammad, the case between me and you has been settled before this came to you. He said: You have spoken the truth. So he stood up and grabbed him by the collar. Abu Jandal shouted at the top of his voice: O group of Muslims, are you sending me back to the polytheists so that they may tempt me in my religion? This increased the evil of the people, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek reward, for God, the Most High, will make a way out and relief for you and for those who are weak with you. We have concluded a peace treaty between us and the people. So we gave them a covenant for that, and they gave us a pledge for it, and we will not betray them.” He said, “So Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, jumped up to him and began walking with Abu Jandal, and he said, ‘Be patient, Abu Jandal, for they are the polytheists, and the blood of one of them is the blood of a dog.’ He said, ‘And the hilt of the sword was close to him.’ He said, ‘I hoped that he would take the sword and strike his father with it.’ He said, ‘The man was jealous of his father.’ He said, ‘And the deal was executed.’ When they had finished writing, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying in the Sacred Sanctuary and he was disturbed in the place of ihram. He said, ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said, “O people, slaughter and shave your heads.” He said, ‘No one stood up.’ He said, ‘Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did the same, but no one stood up.’ He said, ‘Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did the same, but no one stood up.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went back and entered upon Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, and said, ‘O Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?’ She said: O Messenger of God, what you have seen has happened to them, so do not speak to any of them, but go to your sacrificial animal wherever it is, slaughter it and shave your head. If you do that, the people will do the same. So the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out without speaking to anyone until he came to his sacrificial animal, slaughtered it, then sat down and shaved his head. He said: So the people stood up to slaughter and shave their heads, until when he was between Makkah and Madinah, in the middle of the road, Surat Al-Fath was revealed. This is how Ahmad narrated it from this source, and this is how Yunus ibn Bakir and Ziyad Al-Bakka’i narrated it from Abu Ishaq in a similar manner, and in it is strangeness. It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, with a similar chain of transmission, but he differed with him in some matters. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, narrated it in his Sahih, and he presented it in a good and lengthy chain of transmission with good additions. He said in the Book of Conditions of his Sahih: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, al-Zuhri told me, Urwah bin al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of al-Miswar bin Makhrama and Marwan bin al-Hakam, each of them confirming the hadith of the other, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at the time of al-Hudaybiyyah with a few hundred of his companions. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, he put on the sacrificial animal and marked it and entered ihram from it for Umrah. He sent a spy from Khuza’ah and he set out, until when he was at Ghadir al-Ashtaat, his spy came to him and said: The Quraysh have gathered forces against you and they have gathered the Abyssinians against you, and they will fight you, repel you, and prevent you. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Advise me, O people! Do you think we should attack the families and children of those who want to prevent us from the House? In another version: “Do you think we should attack the children of those who helped them? If they come to us, then God will have severed a neck from among the polytheists. Otherwise, we will leave them grieving.” In another version: “If they stay, they will stay resentful, exhausted and exhausted. If they escape, then it will be a neck that God, the Almighty, the Majestic, has severed. Or do you think we should go to the House and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him?” Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, you have set out intentionally for this House, not wanting to kill anyone or wage war. So head towards it, and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him. In another version: Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: God and His Messenger know that we have come as pilgrims and not to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then go. In another version: Proceed in the name of God Almighty. When they were part of the way, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Khalid ibn al-Walid is leading the Quraysh’s cavalry, so take the right. By God, Khalid did not notice them until they were at the rear of the army. He set off running, warning the Quraysh. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued until he was at the pass from which they descended, and his mount knelt. The people said: He has made haste, but she persisted. They said: Al-Qaswa’ has become weak, Al-Qaswa’ has become weak. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Al-Qaswa’ has not become weak, and that is not her nature, but He who restrained the elephant has held her back. Then he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me.” There is no plan in which they glorify the sanctities of God the Most High, except that I give it to them. Then he rebuked her, so she jumped up, so he turned away from them until he descended to the farthest part of Al-Hudaybiyah, on a small place of water that the people were drinking from, but it did not take long for the people to draw water from it, and he complained to the Messenger of God of thirst, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, took out an arrow from his quiver and ordered them to put it in it. By God, he continued to bring them water until they left it. While they were like this, Budayl ibn Warqa' Al-Khuza'i came with a group of his people from Khuza'ah, who were the trustees of the Prophet's (peace and blessings of God be upon him) advice from the people of Tihamah. He said, "I have left Ka'b ibn Lu'ay and 'Amir ibn Lu'ay camped near the waters of Al-Hudaybiyah, with them were the protective amulets. They will fight you and prevent you from reaching the House." The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come to perform Umrah. The Quraysh have been exhausted by war and it has harmed them. If they wish, I will extend their stay for a while and leave me alone with the people. If I prevail, then if they wish to do what the people have done, they may do so, otherwise I have finished. But if they refuse, then by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will fight them over this affair of mine until my forelock is separated or God carries out His command." Budayl said, I will tell them what you say. So he set out until he came to the Quraysh and said, "We have come from this man and we heard him say something. If you wish us to share it with you, we will." Their fools said, We have no need for you to tell us anything about him. Their wise men said, Tell us what you heard him say. He said, I heard him say such and such. So he narrated to them what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said. Then Urwah ibn Mas'ud stood up and said, O people, are you not the father? They said, Yes. He said, Am I not the son? They said, Yes. He said, Do you accuse me? They said, No. He said, Do you not know that I mobilized the people of Ukaz, and when they insisted on me, I came to you with my family, my children and those who obeyed me? They said, Yes. He said, This man has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it and let me come to him. They said: Go to him. So he went to him and began speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl ibn Warqa’. At that, Urwah said: O Muhammad, tell me, if I should eradicate the affair of your people, have you ever heard of anyone among the Arabs who had uprooted their roots before you? If it is the other way around, by God I see faces and I see sects among the people who would flee and leave you. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said to him: Suck the clitoris of Al-Lat, should we flee and leave him? He said: Who is that? They said: Abu Bakr. He said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the favor you had upon me that I did not reward you for, I would have answered you. He said: And he began speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and whenever he spoke to him, he would grab his beard (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah may God be pleased with him was standing over the Prophet’s head (peace and blessings of God be upon him), with a sword and wearing a helmet. Every time Urwah reached for the Prophet’s beard (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he would hit his hand with the scabbard of the sword and say: Take your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Urwah raised his head and said: Who is this? He said: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah. He said: What treachery? Did I not seek your treachery? Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah may God be pleased with him accompanied some people during the pre-Islamic era, killed them, and seized their wealth. Then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: As for Islam, I accept it, but as for wealth, I have no share in it. Then Urwah began to glare at the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said, “By God, whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he wanted. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So Urwah returned to his companions and said, ‘O people! By God, I have visited kings, and I have visited Chosroes, Caesar, and the Negus. By God, I have never seen a king whose companions respect him as much as the companions of Muhammad respect Muhammad. By God, whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he wanted. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him. He has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it.’” A man from Banu Kinanah said, Let me go to him. They said, Go to him. When he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions may God be pleased with them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who venerate sacrificial animals, so send them to him. So they sent them and people met him, chanting the Talbiyah. When he saw that, he said, Glory be to God, it is not appropriate for these people to be prevented from the House. When he returned to his companions, he said, I saw that the sacrificial animals have been girdled and branded, so I do not think they should be prevented from the House. A man from among them called Mukraz ibn Hafs stood up and said, Let me go to him. They said, Go to him. When he came to them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is Mukraz, and he is a wicked man. So he began to speak to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and while he was speaking to him, Suhayl ibn Amr came. Muammar said: Ayyub told me on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: When Suhayl ibn Amr came, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Your matter has been made easy for you. Muammar said: Az-Zuhri said in his hadith: Then Suhayl ibn Amr came and said: Let us write a document between us. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for Ali may God be pleased with him and said: “Write: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Suhayl ibn Amr said: “As for ‘the Most Gracious,’ by God I do not know what it is, but write: In Your name, O God, as you used to write.” The Muslims said: By God, we will not write it except in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Write: In Your name, O God,” then he said: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon. Suhayl said: “By God, if we had known that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you from the House or fought you, but write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: “By God, I am the Messenger of God, even if you call me a liar. Write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah.” Al-Zuhri said: This is because he said: By God, if they ask me for a plan in which they glorify the sacred things of God Almighty, I will give it to them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: On the condition that you leave us alone with the House so that we may circumambulate it. Suhayl said: By God, the Arabs will not say that we were pressured, but that will be next year. So he wrote. Suhayl said: On the condition that if a man from us comes to you, even if he is of your religion, you return him to us. The Muslims said: “Glory be to God. How can he be returned to the polytheists when he came as a Muslim?” While they were like that, Abu Jandal bin Suhayl bin Amr came, swaying in his chains, having come out from the lower part of Mecca and thrown himself down among the Muslims. Suhayl said, O Muhammad, this is the first person I will sue you for, that you return him to me. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, We have not yet concluded the treaty. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Then I will never make peace with you on anything.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Then grant him his due...I will not grant him that. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Yes, do it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, I will not. Mukraz said, Yes, we have granted him his due. Abu Jandal said, O group of Muslims, should I return him to the polytheists when I came to them as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered? He had been severely tortured for the sake of God. Umar may God be pleased with him said, “I came to the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, ‘Are you not truly the Prophet of God?’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Yes.” I said, Are we not on the truth and our enemy on falsehood? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Yes. I said, Then why would we give up our religion? He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, I am the Messenger of God and I will not disobey Him, and He will support me. I said, Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “Yes. Did I tell you that we would come to it this year?” I said, No. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Then you will come to it and circumambulate it. I went to Abu Bakr and said, Are we not truly the Prophet of God? He said, Yes. I said, Are we not upon the truth and our enemy not upon falsehood? He said, Yes. I said, Then why would we give up our religion? He said, O man, he is the Messenger of God and he does not disobey his Lord, and He is his supporter, so hold fast to his roots, for by God, he is upon the truth. I said, Did he not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it? He said, “Yes. Did he tell you that you would come to it this year?” I said, No. He said, Then you will come to it and circumambulate it. Az-Zuhri said: Umar may God be pleased with him said: So I did some work for that. He said: When he had finished writing the book, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions: Get up and slaughter, then shave your head. By God, not a single one of them got up until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said that three times. When none of them got up, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her said to him: O Prophet of God, do you like that? Go out and do not say a word to any of them until you slaughter your sacrifice and call your barber to shave you. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and did not speak to any of them until he had done that. He slaughtered his sacrifice and called his barber to shave him. When they saw that, they stood up and slaughtered their sacrifices, and some of them began shaving each other’s heads until some of them almost killed each other out of grief. Then believing women came to him, and God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, until he reached with the protection of the disbelieving women. So Omar, may God be pleased with him, divorced two of his wives who had been polytheists on that day, and he married one of them, Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other, Safwan ibn Umayya. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned to Madinah, and Abu Basir, a man from the Quraysh who was a Muslim, came to him. They sent two men after him and said, The covenant that you made with us. He gave it to the two men, and they went out with it until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah. They stopped and ate some of their dates. Abu Basir said to one of the two men, By God, I think this sword of yours, so-and-so, is good. The other drew it and said, "Yes, by God, it is good. I have tried it again and again." Abu Basir said, Let me see it. So he gave him control over it and struck it until it became cold. The other ran until he reached Madinah and ran into the mosque. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him, he said, This man saw a panic. When he reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said, By God, my companion has been killed, and I am about to be killed. Abu Basir came and said, "O Messenger of God, by God, God has fulfilled your covenant. You returned me to them, and God saved me from them." The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Woe to his mother, a war-monger if only someone had been with him. When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them, so he went out until he reached Saif al-Bahr. He said, “Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped from them and joined Abu Baseer. No man from Quraysh who had embraced Islam would leave without joining Abu Baseer, until a group of them gathered. By God, they did not hear of a camel going out from Quraysh to Syria without intercepting it, killing them and seizing their wealth. Quraysh sent word to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, urging him by God and kinship to send him to them. Whoever of them came to him was safe. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent word to them, and God, the Almighty, revealed: “And it is He who has restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah” - until he reached - the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance. Their fanaticism was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Messenger of God, nor did they acknowledge In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and they stood between them and the House. This is how al-Bukhari narrated it here. He also included it in his Tafsir, in the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, in the Hajj and elsewhere from the hadith of Muammar and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, both of them from al-Zuhri with it. It was mentioned in some places on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Marwan and Al-Miswar on the authority of men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that, and this is more likely, and God knows best. No one has narrated it more simply than here, and between it and the narration of Ibn Ishaq there are differences in places, and there are benefits that should be added to what is here, and for that reason we have cited that narration and this one, and God is the one sought for help and upon Him we rely, and there is no power or strength except with God, the Almighty, the Wise. Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Sulami narrated to us, Ya’la narrated to us, Abdul Aziz ibn Siyah narrated to us on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit who said: I came to Abu Wa’il to ask him, and he said: We were at Siffin and a man said: Haven’t you seen those who call to the Book of God? Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: Yes. Sahl ibn Hanif said: Accuse yourselves, for I saw us on the day of Hudaybiyyah, meaning the peace treaty that was between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the polytheists. If we had seen fighting, we would have fought. Then Umar may God be pleased with him came and said: Are we not on the truth and they on falsehood? Aren’t our dead in Paradise and theirs in Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Why should we give up our religion and go back before God has judged between us? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Ibn al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of God and God will never let me down. So he went back in anger and could not be patient until he came to Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him and said: O Abu Bakr, aren’t we on the truth and they on falsehood? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, he is the Messenger of God and God will never let him down. So Surat Al-Fath was revealed. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places, and Muslim and Al-Nasa'i through other chains of narration on the authority of Abu Wa'il Sufyan bin Salamah on the authority of Sahl bin Hunaif with it. And in some of its wordings: O people, accuse opinions, for I saw myself on the day of Abu Jandal, and if I had the ability to reject the command of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I would have rejected it. And in another narration: So Surat Al-Fath was revealed, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and recited it to him. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, who said: The Quraysh made peace with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and among them was Suhayl ibn Amr. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ali may God be pleased with him: Write ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.’ Suhayl said: “We do not know what ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ means, but write what we know: ‘In Your name, O God.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Write: From Muhammad, the Messenger of God.” The Prophet said: If we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would follow you, but write your name and your father’s name. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Write: From Muhammad ibn Abdullah.” They stipulated to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever comes from you, we will not return him to you, and whoever comes to you from us, you will return him to us. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Messenger of God, should we write this? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, whoever goes to them from us, God will distance him. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah with this chain of transmission. Ahmad also said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Ammar, who said: Samak told me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When the Kharijites went out, they withdrew, so I said to them: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the polytheists on the day of Hudaybiyyah, so he said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: “Write, Ali, this is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, made peace with.” They said: If we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have fought you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Erase, Ali. O God, You know that I am Your Messenger. Erase, Ali, and write: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah made peace with.” By God, the Messenger of God is better than Ali, and he erased himself, but his erasure did not erase him from the prophethood. Are you excluded from this? They said yes. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar Al-Yamami in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Adam, on the authority of Zuhair bin Harb, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered seventy camels on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah, including a camel for Abu Jahl. When it turned away from the House, it moaned as it moans for its young.
48:26: God the Almighty says, informing us about the infidels among the polytheists of the Quraysh, and about what they did to support them against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: They are the ones who disbelieved meaning they are the infidels and not others, and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque meaning you are more entitled to it and you are its people in fact, and the sacrificial offering was held back from reaching its destination meaning they prevented the sacrificial offering from reaching it, and this is due to their transgression and stubbornness. The sacrificial offering was seventy camels, as will come, God willing. And the Almighty’s saying: And had it not been for believing men and believing women meaning among them who conceal their faith and hide it from them, fearing for themselves from their people, We would have given you power over them, so you would have killed them and destroyed their greenery. But among their courtyards, among the believing men and believing women, are people whom you do not know when they are being killed. For this reason God the Almighty said: You did not know them, lest you trample them and a disgrace should befall you because of them meaning sin and penalty without knowledge, so that God may admit into His mercy whom He wills. That is, He delays their punishment in order to rid them of the believers, and for many of them to return to Islam. Then the Blessed and Exalted said: If you were to separate that is, if the disbelievers were to be distinguished from the believers among them, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment that is, We would have given you power over them, and you would have killed them in a terrible manner. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Abu al-Zinba’ Ruh ibn al-Faraj narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Ibad al-Makki narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’d, a client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Hajar ibn Khalaf narrated to us, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Awf say: I heard Junayd ibn Sab’ say: I fought the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at the beginning of the day as an unbeliever, and I fought with him at the end of the day as a Muslim, and it was revealed about us: And had it not been for believing men and believing women, he said: We were nine people, seven men and two women. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibad al-Makki with it, and he said in it on the authority of Abu Jumah Junayd ibn Sab’, and he mentioned it. The correct version is Abu Ja’far Habib ibn Sab’a. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Hajar ibn Khalaf with it: He said: We were three men and nine women, and it was revealed about us: And had it not been for believing men and believing women, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari narrated to us. Abdullah bin Othman bin Jabalah told us on the authority of Abu Hamza on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the Almighty’s statement: If they were to separate, We would certainly punish those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment. He said: If the disbelievers were to separate from the believers, God would punish them with a painful punishment by killing them. And the Almighty said: When those who disbelieved put into their hearts arrogance - the arrogance of the times of ignorance that was when they refused to write In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful and they refused to write This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has decreed. So God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of piety which is the saying There is no god but God as Ibn Jarir and Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said. Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah Abu Ali Al-Basri narrated to us, Sufyan bin Habib narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Tufayl, meaning Ibn Abi bin Ka’b, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: And make them adhere to the word of piety. He said: There is no god but God. And this is how Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah, and he said: It is strange. We do not know it except from his hadith. I asked Abu Zur’ah about it, but he did not know it except from this source. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Abdullah bin Saleh narrated to us, Al-Layth narrated to me, Abdul Rahman bin Khalid narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, informed him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but God. Whoever says: There is no god but God, his wealth and his life are protected from me, except for his right, and his reckoning is with God Almighty.” And God revealed in His Book and mentioned a people, saying: “Indeed, when it was said to them: There is no god but God, they were arrogant.” And God Almighty said: His praise: And he made them adhere to the word of piety, and they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it. It is There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. But they were arrogant about it, and the polytheists were arrogant about it on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them regarding the term. Ibn Jarir narrated it with these additions from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, and it appears that it was inserted from the words of Al-Zuhri, and God knows best. Mujahid said: The word of piety is sincerity. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: It is: “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.” Yunus ibn Bakir said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. Ath-Thawri said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God alone, with no partner. Ibn Umar said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God, and God is Great. Ibn Umar said the same, may God be pleased with them both. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the words of God, And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: The testimony that there is no god but God, which is the head of all piety. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, meaning: There is no god but God and jihad in His cause. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: It is: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Muammar said: Ath-Thawri said: And make them adhere to the word of piety, saying: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Qatada said, And He made them adhere to the word of piety. He said, There is no god but God. “And they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it.” The Muslims were more deserving of it and more worthy of it. And God is Knowing of all things. That is, He knows who deserves good and who deserves evil. An-Nasa’i said: Ibrahim ibn Sa’id told us, Shababah ibn Suwar told us, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Ala’ ibn Nuwayr, on the authority of Bishr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, may God be pleased with him, that he used to recite, When those who disbelieved put into their hearts arrogance, the arrogance of the times of ignorance. And if you had been as arrogant as they were, the Sacred Mosque would have been ruined. report of that reached ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, so he spoke harshly to him and said, “You know that I used to go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would teach me from what God had taught him.” ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, said, Rather, you are a man who has knowledge and the Qur’an, so recite and learn from what God and His Messenger have taught you. This is a mention of the hadiths related to the story of Hudaybiyyah and the story of the peace treaty. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn Al-Hakam, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah intending to visit the House, not intending to fight. He brought with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, so each sacrificial animal was for ten. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he was at Usfan, where Bishr ibn Sufyan Al-Ka’bi met him and said: O Messenger of God, these are the Quraysh. They heard of your march, so they went out with them, wearing tiger skins, and they pledged to God Almighty that they would never enter it upon them by force. And here is Khalid ibn Al-Walid with their cavalry, whom they have advanced to Kara’ Al-Ghamim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Woe to the Quraysh! War has consumed them. What would they suffer if they left me alone with the rest of the people? If they defeat me, then what they wanted will happen, and if God Almighty makes me victorious, they will enter Islam in great numbers, and if they do not, they will fight and have strength. So what do the Quraysh think? By God, I will not cease…” I will fight them for that with which God the Almighty has sent me until God the Almighty makes me victorious or this forerunner is left alone.” Then he ordered the people to take the right between the two sides of Al-Hamd on a road that leads out to the pass of Al-Marar and Al-Hudaybiyah from the bottom of Mecca. He said: So he took the army that road, and when the Quraysh cavalry saw that the army had deviated from their path, they galloped back to the Quraysh. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out until he took the pass of Al-Marar, and his she-camel knelt down and the people said: She has not lain down. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “She has not lain down and that is not her nature, but He who held back the elephant from Mecca held her back. By God, if the Quraysh call me today to a plan in which they ask me to maintain kinship ties, I will give it to them.” Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the people, Go down. They said, O Messenger of God, there is no water in this valley for people to go down to. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his companions. He went down into one of those wells and stuck it in it. Water gushed forth until the people drove away from it with sticks. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was at peace, there was Budayl ibn Warqa’ with some men from Khuza’ah. He said to them the same as he had said to Bishr ibn Sufyan. They returned to the Quraysh and said, “O people of Quraysh, you are hastening to punish Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Muhammad did not come to fight, he only came as a visitor to this House and to honor its rights.” So they accused them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Al-Zuhri said: Khuza’a was in the possession of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, both polytheists and Muslims, and they did not hide from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, anything that was in Mecca. They said: If he only came for that purpose, then by God he will never enter it against us by force, and the Arabs will not speak of that. Then they sent to him Mukraz ibn Hafs, one of the Banu Amir ibn Lu’ayy. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: This is a treacherous man. When he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, spoke to him in a manner similar to what he had spoken to his companions. Then he returned to Quraysh and informed them of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, had said to him. They sent to him Al-Hulays ibn Alqama Al-Kinani, who was at that time the chief of the Abyssinians. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: This is from a people who are godless, so send the sacrificial animals. When he saw the sacrificial animals flowing towards him from the width of the valley in their necklaces, their hair having been eaten away by the length of the detention from… His place, he returned and did not reach the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of respect for what he saw, so he said: O people of Quraysh, I have seen something that is not permissible to hang the sacrificial animals in its necklaces, its hair has eaten away from being kept in its place for a long time. They said: Sit down, you are only a Bedouin and you have no knowledge. So they sent to him Urwah ibn Mas`ud Al-Thaqafi who said: O people of Quraysh, I have seen what happens to those you send to Muhammad when he comes to you of abuse and bad language. You know that you are a father and I am a son. I heard about what happened to you, so I gathered those of my people who obeyed me and then came until I consoled you with myself. They said: You have spoken the truth. You are not accused in our eyes. So he went out until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and sat before him and said: O Muhammad, you have gathered the rabble of the people and then you have come to your house to destroy it. It is Quraysh who have come out with the most precious of incantations. They have put on the skins of tigers and pledged to God Almighty that you will never enter it upon them by force. By God, it is as if I see these people fleeing from you tomorrow. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was sitting behind the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: Suck the clitoris of Al-Lat, should we flee from it? He said: Who is this, O Muhammad? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is the son of Abu Quhafah. He said: By God, were it not for the favor you had upon me, I would have rewarded you with it, but for this. Then he grabbed the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah may God be pleased with him was standing over the head of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with iron. He struck his hand and said: “Retain your hand from the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before, by God, it does not reach you.” He said: Woe to you, how rude and coarse you are! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiled. He said: Who is this, O Muhammad? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is your nephew, Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah. He said: “He is treacherous. Did you wash your private parts until yesterday?” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke to him in the same way he had spoken to his companions, and informed him that he had not come intending war. He said: So he got up from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he saw what his companions were doing to him. He did not perform ablution without them rushing to him, nor did he spit without them rushing to him, nor did anything fall from his hair without them taking it. So he returned to the Quraysh and said: O people of Quraysh, I came to Khosrau in his kingdom, and I came to Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms, and by God I have never seen a king like Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his companions. I have seen people who would never surrender him for anything, so follow your opinion. He said: Before that, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had sent Khurash ibn Umayyah Al-Khuza’i to Mecca, and he carried him on his camel called Al-Thalab. When he entered Mecca, the Quraysh attacked him and wanted to kill Khurash, but the Abyssinians prevented them until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He called for Umar may God be pleased with him to send him to Mecca. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from the Quraysh, and there is no one from Banu Adi among them to protect me. The Quraysh know of my enmity towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will guide you to a man who is more honorable among them than I am: Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and sent him to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but had come to visit this House and to respect its sanctity. So Uthman, may God be pleased with him, set out until he reached Mecca, and he was met by Abaan ibn Sa`id ibn al-`As. He got down from his mount and carried him in front of him, made him ride behind him and protected him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Uthman, may God be pleased with him, set out until he reached Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent him with. They said to Uthman, may God be pleased with him, If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: “I would not do that until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulates it.” He said: The Quraysh detained him with them. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Uthman, may God be pleased with him, had been killed. Muhammad said: Al-Zuhri told me that the Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn Amr and said: Go to Muhammad and make peace with him, and do not be lenient in your peace treaty unless he withdraws from us this year. By God, the Arabs will never say that he entered our country by force again. So Suhayl ibn Amr went to him, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: “The people wanted peace when they sent this man.” When he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they spoke at length and went back and forth until peace was concluded between them. When the matter was settled and nothing remained but the written document, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, jumped up and went to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and said: O Abu Bakr, is he not the Messenger of God? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists? He said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give in to contempt in our religion? Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Umar, stick to his planting wherever he is, for I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God. Omar may God be pleased with him said: And I bear witness. Then he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes. He said: Then why should we give in to humiliation in our religion? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I am the servant of God and His Messenger. I will not disobey His command and He will not let me down.” Then Omar may God be pleased with him said: I continued to fast, pray, give charity, and free slaves because of what I did, fearing what I said that day, until I hoped that it would be good. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and said: Write In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Suhayl said: I do not know this, but write: In Your name, O God. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Write in your name, O God. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed to.” Suhayl ibn Amr said to him: “If I testify that you are the Messenger of God, I would not fight you. But write: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah and Suhayl ibn Amr have agreed to, to cease war for ten years, during which people will be safe and will refrain from attacking one another. However, whoever of his companions comes to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, without the permission of his guardian, he will be returned to him. Whoever of those with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes to the Quraysh, they will not return him. There will be a closed bond between us and there will be no chains or shackles. Among their conditions when they wrote the document was that whoever wanted to enter into the contract and covenant of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he will enter into it, and whoever wanted to enter into the contract and covenant of the Quraysh, he will enter into it. Then Khuza’ah rose up and said: We are in the contract and covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Banu Bakr rose up and said: We are in the contract and covenant of the Quraysh. You will withdraw from us this year and not enter Mecca upon us. And when it is the next year, we will leave you and you will enter it with your companions.” I stayed there for three days, with the weapon of a rider. Do not enter it with anything but swords in their scabbards. While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was writing the document, Abu Jandal bin Suhayl bin Amr came to him in chains that had been stolen from him to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had gone out, and they had no doubt about the victory, due to a vision that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had seen. When they saw what they saw of the peace and the return, and what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had endured, the people were deeply troubled by that, until they were about to perish. When Suhayl saw Abu Jandal, he stood up and slapped him in the face. He said: O Muhammad, the case between me and you has been settled before this came to you. He said: You have spoken the truth. So he stood up and grabbed him by the collar. Abu Jandal shouted at the top of his voice: O group of Muslims, are you sending me back to the polytheists so that they may tempt me in my religion? This increased the evil of the people, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek reward, for God, the Most High, will make a way out and relief for you and for those who are weak with you. We have concluded a peace treaty between us and the people. So we gave them a covenant for that, and they gave us a pledge for it, and we will not betray them.” He said, “So Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, jumped up to him and began walking with Abu Jandal, and he said, ‘Be patient, Abu Jandal, for they are the polytheists, and the blood of one of them is the blood of a dog.’ He said, ‘And the hilt of the sword was close to him.’ He said, ‘I hoped that he would take the sword and strike his father with it.’ He said, ‘The man was jealous of his father.’ He said, ‘And the deal was executed.’ When they had finished writing, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying in the Sacred Sanctuary and he was disturbed in the place of ihram. He said, ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said, “O people, slaughter and shave your heads.” He said, ‘No one stood up.’ He said, ‘Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did the same, but no one stood up.’ He said, ‘Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did the same, but no one stood up.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went back and entered upon Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, and said, ‘O Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?’ She said: O Messenger of God, what you have seen has happened to them, so do not speak to any of them, but go to your sacrificial animal wherever it is, slaughter it and shave your head. If you do that, the people will do the same. So the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out without speaking to anyone until he came to his sacrificial animal, slaughtered it, then sat down and shaved his head. He said: So the people stood up to slaughter and shave their heads, until when he was between Makkah and Madinah, in the middle of the road, Surat Al-Fath was revealed. This is how Ahmad narrated it from this source, and this is how Yunus ibn Bakir and Ziyad Al-Bakka’i narrated it from Abu Ishaq in a similar manner, and in it is strangeness. It was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, with a similar chain of transmission, but he differed with him in some matters. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, narrated it in his Sahih, and he presented it in a good and lengthy chain of transmission with good additions. He said in the Book of Conditions of his Sahih: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, al-Zuhri told me, Urwah bin al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of al-Miswar bin Makhrama and Marwan bin al-Hakam, each of them confirming the hadith of the other, they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at the time of al-Hudaybiyyah with a few hundred of his companions. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, he put on the sacrificial animal and marked it and entered ihram from it for Umrah. He sent a spy from Khuza’ah and he set out, until when he was at Ghadir al-Ashtaat, his spy came to him and said: The Quraysh have gathered forces against you and they have gathered the Abyssinians against you, and they will fight you, repel you, and prevent you. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Advise me, O people! Do you think we should attack the families and children of those who want to prevent us from the House? In another version: “Do you think we should attack the children of those who helped them? If they come to us, then God will have severed a neck from among the polytheists. Otherwise, we will leave them grieving.” In another version: “If they stay, they will stay resentful, exhausted and exhausted. If they escape, then it will be a neck that God, the Almighty, the Majestic, has severed. Or do you think we should go to the House and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him?” Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, you have set out intentionally for this House, not wanting to kill anyone or wage war. So head towards it, and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him. In another version: Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: God and His Messenger know that we have come as pilgrims and not to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then go. In another version: Proceed in the name of God Almighty. When they were part of the way, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Khalid ibn al-Walid is leading the Quraysh’s cavalry, so take the right. By God, Khalid did not notice them until they were at the rear of the army. He set off running, warning the Quraysh.
