The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued until he was at the pass from which they descended, and his mount knelt. The people said: He has made haste, but she persisted. They said: Al-Qaswa’ has become weak, Al-Qaswa’ has become weak. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Al-Qaswa’ has not become weak, and that is not her nature, but He who restrained the elephant has held her back. Then he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me.” There is no plan in which they glorify the sanctities of God the Most High, except that I give it to them. Then he rebuked her, so she jumped up, so he turned away from them until he descended to the farthest part of Al-Hudaybiyah, on a small place of water that the people were drinking from, but it did not take long for the people to draw water from it, and he complained to the Messenger of God of thirst, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, took out an arrow from his quiver and ordered them to put it in it. By God, he continued to bring them water until they left it. While they were like this, Budayl ibn Warqa' Al-Khuza'i came with a group of his people from Khuza'ah, who were the trustees of the Prophet's (peace and blessings of God be upon him) advice from the people of Tihamah. He said, "I have left Ka'b ibn Lu'ay and 'Amir ibn Lu'ay camped near the waters of Al-Hudaybiyah, with them were the protective amulets. They will fight you and prevent you from reaching the House." The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come to perform Umrah. The Quraysh have been exhausted by war and it has harmed them. If they wish, I will extend their stay for a while and leave me alone with the people. If I prevail, then if they wish to do what the people have done, they may do so, otherwise I have finished. But if they refuse, then by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will fight them over this affair of mine until my forelock is separated or God carries out His command." Budayl said, I will tell them what you say. So he set out until he came to the Quraysh and said, "We have come from this man and we heard him say something. If you wish us to share it with you, we will." Their fools said, We have no need for you to tell us anything about him. Their wise men said, Tell us what you heard him say. He said, I heard him say such and such. So he narrated to them what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said. Then Urwah ibn Mas'ud stood up and said, O people, are you not the father? They said, Yes. He said, Am I not the son? They said, Yes. He said, Do you accuse me? They said, No. He said, Do you not know that I mobilized the people of Ukaz, and when they insisted on me, I came to you with my family, my children and those who obeyed me? They said, Yes. He said, This man has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it and let me come to him. They said: Go to him. So he went to him and began speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl ibn Warqa’. At that, Urwah said: O Muhammad, tell me, if I should eradicate the affair of your people, have you ever heard of anyone among the Arabs who had uprooted their roots before you? If it is the other way around, by God I see faces and I see sects among the people who would flee and leave you. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said to him: Suck the clitoris of Al-Lat, should we flee and leave him? He said: Who is that? They said: Abu Bakr. He said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the favor you had upon me that I did not reward you for, I would have answered you. He said: And he began speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and whenever he spoke to him, he would grab his beard (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah may God be pleased with him was standing over the Prophet’s head (peace and blessings of God be upon him), with a sword and wearing a helmet. Every time Urwah reached for the Prophet’s beard (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he would hit his hand with the scabbard of the sword and say: Take your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Urwah raised his head and said: Who is this? He said: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah. He said: What treachery? Did I not seek your treachery? Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah may God be pleased with him accompanied some people during the pre-Islamic era, killed them, and seized their wealth. Then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: As for Islam, I accept it, but as for wealth, I have no share in it. Then Urwah began to glare at the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said, “By God, whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he wanted. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So Urwah returned to his companions and said, ‘O people! By God, I have visited kings, and I have visited Chosroes, Caesar, and the Negus. By God, I have never seen a king whose companions respect him as much as the companions of Muhammad respect Muhammad. By God, whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he wanted. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him. He has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it.’” A man from Banu Kinanah said, Let me go to him. They said, Go to him. When he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions may God be pleased with them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who venerate sacrificial animals, so send them to him. So they sent them and people met him, chanting the Talbiyah. When he saw that, he said, Glory be to God, it is not appropriate for these people to be prevented from the House. When he returned to his companions, he said, I saw that the sacrificial animals have been girdled and branded, so I do not think they should be prevented from the House. A man from among them called Mukraz ibn Hafs stood up and said, Let me go to him. They said, Go to him. When he came to them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is Mukraz, and he is a wicked man. So he began to speak to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and while he was speaking to him, Suhayl ibn Amr came. Muammar said: Ayyub told me on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: When Suhayl ibn Amr came, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Your matter has been made easy for you. Muammar said: Az-Zuhri said in his hadith: Then Suhayl ibn Amr came and said: Let us write a document between us. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for Ali may God be pleased with him and said: “Write: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” Suhayl ibn Amr said: “As for ‘the Most Gracious,’ by God I do not know what it is, but write: In Your name, O God, as you used to write.” The Muslims said: By God, we will not write it except in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Write: In Your name, O God,” then he said: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon. Suhayl said: “By God, if we had known that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you from the House or fought you, but write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: “By God, I am the Messenger of God, even if you call me a liar. Write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah.” Al-Zuhri said: This is because he said: By God, if they ask me for a plan in which they glorify the sacred things of God Almighty, I will give it to them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: On the condition that you leave us alone with the House so that we may circumambulate it. Suhayl said: By God, the Arabs will not say that we were pressured, but that will be next year. So he wrote. Suhayl said: On the condition that if a man from us comes to you, even if he is of your religion, you return him to us. The Muslims said: “Glory be to God. How can he be returned to the polytheists when he came as a Muslim?” While they were like that, Abu Jandal bin Suhayl bin Amr came, swaying in his chains, having come out from the lower part of Mecca and thrown himself down among the Muslims. Suhayl said, O Muhammad, this is the first person I will sue you for, that you return him to me. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, We have not yet concluded the treaty. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Then I will never make peace with you on anything.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Then grant him his due...I will not grant him that. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Yes, do it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, I will not. Mukraz said, Yes, we have granted him his due. Abu Jandal said, O group of Muslims, should I return him to the polytheists when I came to them as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered? He had been severely tortured for the sake of God. Umar may God be pleased with him said, “I came to the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, ‘Are you not truly the Prophet of God?’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Yes.” I said, Are we not on the truth and our enemy on falsehood? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Yes. I said, Then why would we give up our religion? He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, I am the Messenger of God and I will not disobey Him, and He will support me. I said, Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, “Yes. Did I tell you that we would come to it this year?” I said, No. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, Then you will come to it and circumambulate it. I went to Abu Bakr and said, Are we not truly the Prophet of God? He said, Yes. I said, Are we not upon the truth and our enemy not upon falsehood? He said, Yes. I said, Then why would we give up our religion? He said, O man, he is the Messenger of God and he does not disobey his Lord, and He is his supporter, so hold fast to his roots, for by God, he is upon the truth. I said, Did he not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it? He said, “Yes. Did he tell you that you would come to it this year?” I said, No. He said, Then you will come to it and circumambulate it. Az-Zuhri said: Umar may God be pleased with him said: So I did some work for that. He said: When he had finished writing the book, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions: Get up and slaughter, then shave your head. By God, not a single one of them got up until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said that three times. When none of them got up, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her said to him: O Prophet of God, do you like that? Go out and do not say a word to any of them until you slaughter your sacrifice and call your barber to shave you. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and did not speak to any of them until he had done that. He slaughtered his sacrifice and called his barber to shave him. When they saw that, they stood up and slaughtered their sacrifices, and some of them began shaving each other’s heads until some of them almost killed each other out of grief. Then believing women came to him, and God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, until he reached with the protection of the disbelieving women. So Omar, may God be pleased with him, divorced two of his wives who had been polytheists on that day, and he married one of them, Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other, Safwan ibn Umayya. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned to Madinah, and Abu Basir, a man from the Quraysh who was a Muslim, came to him. They sent two men after him and said, The covenant that you made with us. He gave it to the two men, and they went out with it until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah. They stopped and ate some of their dates. Abu Basir said to one of the two men, By God, I think this sword of yours, so-and-so, is good. The other drew it and said, "Yes, by God, it is good. I have tried it again and again." Abu Basir said, Let me see it. So he gave him control over it and struck it until it became cold. The other ran until he reached Madinah and ran into the mosque. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him, he said, This man saw a panic. When he reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said, By God, my companion has been killed, and I am about to be killed. Abu Basir came and said, "O Messenger of God, by God, God has fulfilled your covenant. You returned me to them, and God saved me from them." The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Woe to his mother, a war-monger if only someone had been with him. When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them, so he went out until he reached Saif al-Bahr. He said, “Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped from them and joined Abu Baseer. No man from Quraysh who had embraced Islam would leave without joining Abu Baseer, until a group of them gathered. By God, they did not hear of a camel going out from Quraysh to Syria without intercepting it, killing them and seizing their wealth. Quraysh sent word to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, urging him by God and kinship to send him to them. Whoever of them came to him was safe. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent word to them, and God, the Almighty, revealed: “And it is He who has restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah” - until he reached - the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance. Their fanaticism was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Messenger of God, nor did they acknowledge In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and they stood between them and the House. This is how al-Bukhari narrated it here. He also included it in his Tafsir, in the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, in the Hajj and elsewhere from the hadith of Muammar and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, both of them from al-Zuhri with it. It was mentioned in some places on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Marwan and Al-Miswar on the authority of men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that, and this is more likely, and God knows best. No one has narrated it more simply than here, and between it and the narration of Ibn Ishaq there are differences in places, and there are benefits that should be added to what is here, and for that reason we have cited that narration and this one, and God is the one sought for help and upon Him we rely, and there is no power or strength except with God, the Almighty, the Wise. Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Sulami narrated to us, Ya’la narrated to us, Abdul Aziz ibn Siyah narrated to us on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit who said: I came to Abu Wa’il to ask him, and he said: We were at Siffin and a man said: Haven’t you seen those who call to the Book of God? Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: Yes. Sahl ibn Hanif said: Accuse yourselves, for I saw us on the day of Hudaybiyyah, meaning the peace treaty that was between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the polytheists. If we had seen fighting, we would have fought. Then Umar may God be pleased with him came and said: Are we not on the truth and they on falsehood? Aren’t our dead in Paradise and theirs in Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Why should we give up our religion and go back before God has judged between us? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Ibn al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of God and God will never let me down. So he went back in anger and could not be patient until he came to Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him and said: O Abu Bakr, aren’t we on the truth and they on falsehood? He said: O Ibn Al-Khattab, he is the Messenger of God and God will never let him down. So Surat Al-Fath was revealed. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places, and Muslim and Al-Nasa'i through other chains of narration on the authority of Abu Wa'il Sufyan bin Salamah on the authority of Sahl bin Hunaif with it. And in some of its wordings: O people, accuse opinions, for I saw myself on the day of Abu Jandal, and if I had the ability to reject the command of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I would have rejected it. And in another narration: So Surat Al-Fath was revealed, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called for Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and recited it to him. So he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Umrah the following year and entered it as he had made peace with them. When he had stayed there for three days, they ordered him to leave, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left. This is also in Sahih Muslim. Al-Bukhari also said: Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated to us from Isra’il from Abu Ishaq from Al-Bara’ may God be pleased with him who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Umrah in Dhul-Qa’dah, but the people of Mecca refused to let him enter Mecca until he made a deal with them that they would stay there for three days. When they wrote the deal, they wrote: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed with us. They said: We do not acknowledge this, and if we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you at all. But you are Muhammad bin Abdullah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I am the Messenger of God and I am Muhammad bin Abdullah. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him: Erase the name of the Messenger of God. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No, by God, I will never erase you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the deal, though he was not good at writing, so he wrote: This is what Muhammad bin Abdullah has agreed with us: that he will not enter Mecca with weapons except with a sword in a scabbard, that he will not leave any of its people who wish to follow him, and that he will not prevent any of his companions if they wish to stay there. When he entered her and the time limit had passed, they came to Ali and said: Tell your companion to leave us, for the time limit has passed. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and the daughter of Hamza may God be pleased with him followed him calling: O uncle, O uncle. Ali may God be pleased with him took her and took her by the hand and said to Fatimah may God be pleased with her: Take your cousin. So she carried her. Ali, Zaid and Ja’far may God be pleased with them disputed over her. Ali may God be pleased with him said: I took her, and she is my cousin. Ja’far may God be pleased with him said: My cousin, and her aunt is under me. Zaid may God be pleased with him said: My brother’s daughter. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled in her favor with her aunt and said: The aunt is in the position of the mother. He said to Ali may God be pleased with him: You are from me and I am from you. He said to Ja’far may God be pleased with him: You resemble me in appearance and character. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Zaid may God be pleased with him: You are our brother and our master. Ali may God be pleased with him said: Why don’t you marry the daughter of Hamza may God be pleased with him? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: She is my foster brother’s daughter. This is unique in its chain of transmission. God the Almighty said: Then He knew that which you did not know, and He ordained, before that, a near conquest. That is, God the Almighty knew of the good and benefit in turning you away from Mecca and entering it that year, what you did not know. Then He ordained, before that, that is, before your entry, which you were promised in the vision of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a near conquest, which is the peace that was between you and your enemies from among the polytheists. Then God the Almighty said, giving good tidings to the believers of the victory of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, over his enemy and over all the people of the earth: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that is, with beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. For the Shari’ah includes two things: knowledge and action. Shari’ah knowledge is correct, and Shari’ah action is acceptable. Its narrations are true and its writings are just. That He may make it prevail over all religions, that is, over the people of all religions from all over the earth, from Arabs and non-Arabs, from Muslims and polytheists. And sufficient is God as Witness, that is, He is His Messenger and He is His Supporter. And God the Almighty knows best.

And he narrated it in other places, and Muslim and An-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. He also said: Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us that he heard Ibn Abi Awfa say: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Umrah, we screened him from the young boys of the polytheists and from them, lest they harm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This was reported by Al-Bukhari alone, not by Muslim. Al-Bukhari also said: Muhammad ibn Rafi’ told us, Surayj ibn Al-Nu’man told us, Falih told us, and Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim told me, my father told us, Falih ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to perform Umrah, and the infidels of Quraysh prevented him from reaching the House, so he slaughtered his sacrificial animal and shaved his head at Al-Hudaibiyah and made a deal with them that he would perform Umrah the following year, and that he would not carry any weapons against them except swords, and that he would not stay there except as long as they liked. So he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Umrah the following year and entered it as he had made peace with them. When he had stayed there for three days, they ordered him to leave, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left. This is also in Sahih Muslim. Al-Bukhari also said: Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated to us from Isra’il from Abu Ishaq from Al-Bara’ may God be pleased with him who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Umrah in Dhul-Qa’dah, but the people of Mecca refused to let him enter Mecca until he made a deal with them that they would stay there for three days. When they wrote the deal, they wrote: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed with us. They said: We do not acknowledge this, and if we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you at all. But you are Muhammad bin Abdullah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I am the Messenger of God and I am Muhammad bin Abdullah. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him: Erase the name of the Messenger of God. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No, by God, I will never erase you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the deal, though he was not good at writing, so he wrote: This is what Muhammad bin Abdullah has agreed with us: that he will not enter Mecca with weapons except with a sword in a scabbard, that he will not leave any of its people who wish to follow him, and that he will not prevent any of his companions if they wish to stay there. When he entered her and the time limit had passed, they came to Ali and said: Tell your companion to leave us, for the time limit has passed. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and the daughter of Hamza may God be pleased with him followed him calling: O uncle, O uncle. Ali may God be pleased with him took her and took her by the hand and said to Fatimah may God be pleased with her: Take your cousin. So she carried her. Ali, Zaid and Ja’far may God be pleased with them disputed over her. Ali may God be pleased with him said: I took her, and she is my cousin. Ja’far may God be pleased with him said: My cousin, and her aunt is under me. Zaid may God be pleased with him said: My brother’s daughter. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled in her favor with her aunt and said: The aunt is in the position of the mother. He said to Ali may God be pleased with him: You are from me and I am from you. He said to Ja’far may God be pleased with him: You resemble me in appearance and character. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Zaid may God be pleased with him: You are our brother and our master. Ali may God be pleased with him said: Why don’t you marry the daughter of Hamza may God be pleased with him? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: She is my foster brother’s daughter. This is unique in its chain of transmission. God the Almighty said: Then He knew that which you did not know, and He ordained, before that, a near conquest. That is, God the Almighty knew of the good and benefit in turning you away from Mecca and entering it that year, what you did not know. Then He ordained, before that, that is, before your entry, which you were promised in the vision of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a near conquest, which is the peace that was between you and your enemies from among the polytheists. Then God the Almighty said, giving good tidings to the believers of the victory of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, over his enemy and over all the people of the earth: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that is, with beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. For the Shari’ah includes two things: knowledge and action. Shari’ah knowledge is correct, and Shari’ah action is acceptable. Its narrations are true and its writings are just. That He may make it prevail over all religions, that is, over the people of all religions from all over the earth, from Arabs and non-Arabs, from Muslims and polytheists. And sufficient is God as Witness, that is, He is His Messenger and He is His Supporter. And God the Almighty knows best.
48:29: God the Almighty tells us about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is truly His Messenger, without a doubt or suspicion. He said: Muhammad is the Messenger of God. This is a subject and predicate, and it includes every beautiful description. Then He praised his companions, may God be pleased with them, and said: And those with him are harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. As the Almighty said: Then God will bring forth a people He will love and who will love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers. This is the characteristic of the believers, that one of them should be harsh and violent toward the disbelievers, merciful and kind to the good, angry and frowning at the disbelievers, and smiling and cheerful toward his believing brother, as the Almighty said: O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you and let them find in you harshness. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of the believers in their mutual love and mercy is like that of a single body. If one part of it is ill, the rest of the body feels feverish and sleepless.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The believer to the believer is like a building, whose parts support one another. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, interlocked his fingers. Both hadiths are in Sahih. And the saying of God the Most High: You will see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from God and [His] pleasure. He described them as having much work and much prayer, which is the best of deeds. He described them as being sincere in it to God the Almighty and seeking reward from God the Almighty for the abundant reward, which is Paradise, which includes the bounty of God the Almighty, which is the ample provision for them and His pleasure with them. This is greater than the first, as He the Most High said: And the pleasure of God is greater. And His saying the Most High: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them: Their mark is on their faces meaning good appearance. Mujahid and others said: It means humility and modesty. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Hussain al-Ja'fi told us on the authority of Za'idah on the authority of Mansour on the authority of Mujahid: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration. He said: Humility. I said: I did not see it as anything other than this mark on the face. He said: Perhaps there was before my eyes someone whose heart was harder than Pharaoh. Al-Suddi said: Prayer improves their faces. Some of the early Muslims said: Whoever prays frequently at night, his face will be beautiful during the day. Ibn Majah included this in his Sunan on the authority of Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Talhi, on the authority of Thabit ibn Musa, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays frequently at night, his face will be beautiful during the day. The correct version is that it is a continuation of the hadith. Some of them said: A good deed brings light to the heart, radiance to the face, abundance in provision, and love in people’s hearts. The Commander of the Faithful, Uthman may God be pleased with him said: No one keeps a secret except that God reveals it on his face and through the slips of his tongue. The point is that what is hidden in the soul appears on one’s face. So, if the believer’s secret is sound with God, God will reform his outward appearance to people, as narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him who said: Whoever reforms his secret, God will reform his outward appearance. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mahmud ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi told us, Hamid ibn Adam al-Marwazi told us, al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah al-Arzami, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Jundub ibn Sufyan al-Bajali may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No one keeps a secret except that God dresses him in its garment, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. Al-Arzami is rejected. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If one of you were to work in a solid rock that had no door or window, his work would be revealed to the people, whatever it was. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Zuhair told us, Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan told us that his father told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Indeed, good guidance, good conduct, and moderation are a part of twenty-five parts of prophethood. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Nufaili on the authority of Zuhair on his authority. So the Companions, may God be pleased with them, had pure intentions and good deeds, so everyone who looked at them was impressed by their conduct and guidance. Malik may God be pleased with him said: It has reached me that when the Christians saw the Companions may God be pleased with them who conquered the Levant, they would say: By God, these are better than the disciples, as far as we have been informed. And they were right in that, for this nation is honored in the previous books, and the greatest and best of them are the Companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). God, the Blessed and Exalted, has mentioned them in the revealed books and the circulated reports. That is why He, the Most High, said here: That is their example in the Torah. Then He said: And their example in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot, meaning its young ones, and strengthens it, meaning it makes it strong, and it becomes thick, meaning it grows long and tall, and stands firmly on its stalk, delighting the sowers, meaning, the Companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) supported him, aided him, and aided him, so they are with him like the shoot with the seed, that He may enrage the disbelievers thereby. From this verse, Imam Malik may God have mercy on him extracted, in a narration from him, the excommunication of the Rafidis who hate the Companions may God be pleased with them. He said: Because they annoy them, and whoever annoys the Companions may God be pleased with them is an unbeliever because of this verse. A group of scholars may God be pleased with them agreed with him on this. The hadiths about the virtues of the Companions may God be pleased with them and the prohibition of insulting them are many. God’s praise of them and His pleasure with them is sufficient for them. Then God the Blessed and Exalted said: God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them – this is to clarify the type – forgiveness for their sins and a great reward – meaning a generous reward and noble provision. God’s promise is true and true, and He does not break or change it. Everyone who follows in the footsteps of the Companions may God be pleased with them is under their ruling, and they have virtue, precedence, and perfection that no one else in this nation can reach. May God be pleased with them and satisfy them and make the Gardens of Paradise their abode, and He did. Muslim said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not revile my companions, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equivalent to Mount Uhud, he would not reach the level of one of them, or even half of it. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Fath. All praise and thanks are due to God.
